lessons.title: Multiple Choice Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • One degree equals pi divided by 180 radians, about 0.01745 radian, and a full circle is 2 pi radians.
  • The metric prefix micro stands for 10 to the power minus 6, that is 0.000001.
  • In subtraction the absolute uncertainties add, so a temperature difference of 30 degrees C from two readings each uncertain by 0.5 degrees C carries an uncertainty of 1 degree C.
  • In multiplication and division the percentage uncertainties add, and for a power the percentage uncertainty is multiplied by the power.
  • The number 0.00708600 has six significant figures, because leading zeros are not significant but captive and trailing zeros are.
  • An addition result is rounded to the least number of decimal places, while a multiplication result is rounded to the least number of significant figures.
  • The precision of a measurement is fixed by the place of its last readable significant digit, so 385,000 km is precise to 1000 km.
  • Torque has dimensions M L squared T to the power minus 2, while strain, refractive index and magnification are dimensionless.

Solved Exercises

Exercise - Multiple Choice Questions

Q: Q1. What is the radian measure between the arms of watch at 5:00 pm?

Options: (a) 1 radian (b) 2 radian (c) 3 radian (d) 4 radian

Correct answer: 3 radian

Q: Q2. 1 degree = __________

Options: (a) 0.01745 radian (b) 1 radian (c) 3.14 radian (d) 2 pi radian

Correct answer: 0.01745 radian

Q: Q3. The metric prefix for 0.000001 is

Options: (a) hecto (b) micro (c) deca (d) nano

Correct answer: micro

Q: Q4. Which of the following is the CORRECT way of writing units?

Options: (a) 71 Newton (b) 12 m mu s (c) 8 Kg (d) 43 kg m^-3

Correct answer: 43 kg m^-3

Q: Q5. A student measures a distance several times. The readings lie between 49.8 cm and 50.2 cm. This measurement is best recorded as

Options: (a) (49.8 +- 0.2) cm (b) (49.8 +- 0.4) cm (c) (50.0 +- 0.2) cm (d) (50.0 +- 0.4) cm

Correct answer: (50.0 +- 0.2) cm

Q: Q6. The percent uncertainty in the measurement of (3.76 +- 0.25) m is

Options: (a) 4% (b) 6.6% (c) 25% (d) 376%

Correct answer: 6.6%

Q: Q7. The temperatures of two bodies measured by a thermometer are t_1 = (20 +- 0.5) degrees C and t_2 = (50 +- 0.5) degrees C. The temperature difference and the error therein is

Options: (a) (30 +- 0.0) degrees C (b) (30 +- 0.5) degrees C (c) (30 +- 1) degrees C (d) (30 +- 1.5) degrees C

Correct answer: (30 +- 1) degrees C

Q: Q8. (5.0 m +- 4.0%) x (3.0 s +- 3.3%) =

Options: (a) 15.0 m s +- 13.2% (b) 15.0 m s +- 7.3% (c) 15.0 m s +- 0.7% (d) 15.0 m s +- 15.3%

Correct answer: 15.0 m s +- 7.3%

Q: Q9. (2.0 m +- 2.0%)^3 =

Options: (a) 8.0 m^3 +- 1.0% (b) 8.0 m^3 +- 2.0% (c) 8.0 m^3 +- 5.0% (d) 8.0 m^3 +- 6.0%

Correct answer: 8.0 m^3 +- 6.0%

Q: Q10. The number of significant figures in measurement of 0.00708600 cm are

Options: (a) 3 (b) 4 (c) 6 (d) 9

Correct answer: 6

Q: Q11. How many significant figures does 1.362 + 25.2 have?

Options: (a) 2 (b) 3 (c) 5 (d) 8

Correct answer: 3

Q: Q12. Compute the result to correct number of significant digits 1.513 m + 27.3 m =

Options: (a) 29 m (b) 28.8 m (c) 28.81 m (d) 28.813 m

Correct answer: 28.8 m

Q: Q13. If 7.635 and 4.81 are two significant numbers. Their multiplication in significant digits is:

Options: (a) 36.72435 (b) 36.724 (c) 36.72 (d) 36.7

Correct answer: 36.7

Q: Q14. The precision of the measurement 385,000 km is

Options: (a) 10 km (b) 100 km (c) 1000 km (d) 1000000 km

Correct answer: 1000 km

Q: Q15. [M^0 L^0 T^0] are dimension of

Options: (a) strain (b) refractive index (c) magnification (d) All of these

Correct answer: All of these

Q: Q16. The dimensions of torque are

Options: (a) [M L T] (b) [M^2 L^2 T] (c) [M L^2 T^-2] (d) [M L^2 T^2]

Correct answer: [M L^2 T^-2]

mcqs.why: One degree is 1/360 of a full turn, and a full turn is 2 pi radians, so 1 degree equals 2 pi divided by 360, which is pi divided by 180, about 0.01745 radian.

mcqs.q: The metric prefix for 0.000001 is
mcqs.why: The prefix for one millionth, 10 to the power minus 6 or 0.000001, is micro; hecto means 100, deca means 10 and nano means 10 to the power minus 9.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is the CORRECT way of writing units?
mcqs.why: Unit names are written in lower case with a space after the number, and symbols for compound units use negative powers, so the density written with kilogram and metre to the power minus 3 follows every SI convention.

mcqs.q: A student measures a distance several times. The readings lie between 49.8 cm and 50.2 cm. This measurement is best recorded as
mcqs.why: Readings spread from 49.8 cm to 50.2 cm, so the central value is 50.0 cm and the spread on either side is 0.2 cm, giving the recording 50.0 plus or minus 0.2 cm.

mcqs.q: The percent uncertainty in the measurement of (3.76 +- 0.25) m is
mcqs.why: Percentage uncertainty equals the absolute uncertainty divided by the measured value, times 100: 0.25 divided by 3.76 times 100 is about 6.65 percent, which rounds to 6.6 percent.

mcqs.q: The temperatures of two bodies measured by a thermometer are t_1 = (20 +- 0.5) degrees C and t_2 = (50 +- 0.5) degrees C. The temperature difference and the error therein is
mcqs.why: The difference is 50 minus 20, which is 30 degrees C, and in subtraction the absolute uncertainties add, so 0.5 plus 0.5 gives an uncertainty of 1 degree C.
The product is 5.0 times 3.0, which is 15.0, and in multiplication the percentage uncertainties add: 4.0 percent plus 3.3 percent gives 7.3 percent total uncertainty.
Cubing means the quantity is multiplied by itself three times, so the percentage uncertainty is multiplied by the power 3: 3 times 2.0 percent gives 6.0 percent on the volume 8.0 cubic metres.

mcqs.q: The number of significant figures in measurement of 0.00708600 cm are
mcqs.why: Leading zeros are never significant, while the zeros between non-zero digits and the trailing zeros after them are significant: 7, 0, 8, 6, 0 and 0 give six significant figures.

mcqs.q: How many significant figures does 1.362 + 25.2 have?
mcqs.why: The sum 1.362 plus 25.2 is 26.562, which must be rounded to one decimal place because 25.2 has one decimal place; 26.6 therefore contains three significant figures.

mcqs.q: Compute the result to correct number of significant digits 1.513 m + 27.3 m =
mcqs.why: Adding gives 1.513 plus 27.3 equals 28.813, and an addition result is rounded to the least number of decimal places, one place from 27.3, giving 28.8 metres.

mcqs.q: If 7.635 and 4.81 are two significant numbers. Their multiplication in significant digits is:
mcqs.why: The product is 7.635 times 4.81, which equals 36.72435, and a multiplication result keeps the least number of significant figures, three from 4.81, giving 36.7.

mcqs.q: The precision of the measurement 385,000 km is
mcqs.why: Precision is set by the place of the last significant digit that can be read; in 385,000 km that digit sits in the thousands place, so the measurement is precise to 1000 km.

mcqs.q: [M^0 L^0 T^0] are dimension of
mcqs.why: Strain is a ratio of two lengths, refractive index is a ratio of two speeds and magnification is a ratio of two lengths, so each is a pure number with dimensions M0 L0 T0.

mcqs.q: The dimensions of torque are
mcqs.why: Torque is force times perpendicular distance, so its dimensions are mass times length per time squared, times length, giving M L squared T to the power minus 2.

lessons.title: Conceptual Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • A physical quantity is a number multiplied by a unit, and the number alone is meaningless because the same number stands for very different amounts in different units.
  • SI is a single, coherent, decimal and universally accepted system whose derived units come directly from its base units without extra numerical factors.
  • The full plane angle around a circle is 2 pi radians and the full solid angle around a sphere is 4 pi steradians.
  • Least count error comes from the resolution of the instrument and is reduced by using an instrument of smaller least count and by averaging repeated readings.
  • Digits beyond the significant figures are not known reliably, so writing more of them does not increase the accuracy of a result.
  • The precision of a measurement is determined by the least count of the instrument, shown by the position of the last significant digit.
  • Quantities of different dimensions can be multiplied and divided, but only quantities with the same dimensions can be added or subtracted.
  • A dimensionally correct equation is not necessarily a correct equation, because dimensional analysis cannot check dimensionless numerical factors.

Solved Exercises

Exercise - Conceptual Questions

Q: Q1. For an answer to be complete, the units need to be specified. Why?

Ans: A physical quantity is a number multiplied by a unit. The number alone has no meaning, because the same number means completely different amounts in different units: for example, a length of 5 is very different as 5 mm, 5 m or 5 km. The unit tells what standard the number is compared with, so a measurement is complete and can be understood and used by others only when its unit is stated with it.

Q: Q2. What are the advantages of using International System of Units (SI)?

Ans: SI is a single, coherent and universally accepted system, so scientists all over the world understand each other's measurements without conversion confusion. All its units are interrelated (derived units come directly from base units without extra numerical factors), it is decimal based, so changing from one size of unit to another is easy, and it covers every branch of science and technology with the same set of units.

Q: Q3. How many radians account for circumference of a circle? How many steradians account for circumference of a sphere?

Ans: For a circle, the angle at the centre for the full circumference is circumference / radius = 2 pi r / r = 2 pi radians (about 6.28 rad). For a sphere, the solid angle at the centre for the whole surface is surface area / radius squared = 4 pi r^2 / r^2 = 4 pi steradians (about 12.56 sr).

Q: Q4. What is least count error? How can least count error be reduced?

Ans: Least count error is the error associated with the resolution (least count) of the instrument: a measurement cannot be read finer than the smallest division the instrument can show, so every reading carries an uncertainty of about one least count. It is a random type of error. It can be reduced by using an instrument of smaller least count (finer divisions), for example a vernier callipers instead of a metre rule, and by taking repeated readings and averaging them.

Q: Q5. Why including more digits in answers, does not make it more accurate?

Ans: The accuracy of a result is limited by the accuracy of the measurements used, not by the number of digits written. Digits beyond the significant figures are not known reliably; they only come from the calculator and carry no real information about the quantity. Writing them only gives a false impression of accuracy, so a result must be rounded to the correct number of significant figures.

Q: Q6. What determines the precision of a measurement?

Ans: Precision is determined by the least count (resolution) of the measuring instrument, that is, the position of the last significant digit that can be read. The smaller the least count, the more precise the measurement: a measurement of 385,000 km read to the thousands place has a precision of 1000 km, while an instrument with finer divisions gives a value precise to a smaller amount.

Q: Q7. If two quantities have different dimensions, is it possible to multiply and/or divide. Can we add and/or subtract them?

Ans: Yes, quantities of different dimensions can be multiplied and divided; the result simply has the combined dimensions, for example length divided by time gives velocity [L T^-1], and mass multiplied by acceleration gives force. But they cannot be added or subtracted: only quantities with the same dimensions can be added or subtracted, because addition means combining amounts of the same kind.

Q: Q8. The human pulse and the swing of a pendulum are possible time units. Why are they not often used?

Ans: A good unit must be constant, reproducible and the same everywhere. The human pulse rate changes from person to person and with health, age and activity, and the period of a pendulum changes with its length and with the value of g at the place. Because neither is invariable or universally reproducible, they cannot serve as reliable standards of time and are not used.

Q: Q9. If an equation is dimensionally correct, is that equation a right equation?

Ans: Not necessarily. Dimensional correctness is a necessary condition but not a sufficient one. A dimensionally correct equation may still be physically wrong, because dimensional analysis cannot detect wrong numerical factors (such as 1/2 or 2 pi) and cannot distinguish between different quantities that have the same dimensions, such as torque and energy. But a dimensionally wrong equation is certainly wrong.

mcqs.q: Why must a unit always be stated with the number in a measurement?
options: Because a larger unit always gives a larger number
Because the same number means completely different amounts in different units, so the number alone has no definite meaning
Because units are needed only when converting between systems
Because every physical quantity must be written in SI base units only
mcqs.why: A measurement is a number multiplied by a unit, and the unit tells what standard the number is compared with; a length of 5 is very different as 5 mm, 5 m or 5 km, so without the unit the answer is incomplete and cannot be understood by others.

mcqs.q: Which statement gives a correct advantage of the SI system?
options: Its units change from country to country so local work is easier
Its derived units need extra numerical factors to connect them
It is a single coherent decimal system understood worldwide, with derived units formed directly from base units
It covers only mechanics and heat
mcqs.why: SI is universally accepted so scientists everywhere understand each other's measurements, its units are interrelated with derived units coming directly from base units without extra factors, and being decimal based it makes changing unit size easy across every branch of science.

mcqs.q: How many radians are there in the full angle around the centre of a circle?
mcqs.why: The angle at the centre for the full circumference is circumference divided by radius, which is 2 pi r divided by r, giving 2 pi radians, about 6.28 rad, for one complete turn.

mcqs.q: How many steradians are there in the full solid angle around the centre of a sphere?
mcqs.why: The solid angle for the whole surface of a sphere is surface area divided by radius squared, which is 4 pi r squared divided by r squared, giving 4 pi steradians, about 12.56 sr.

mcqs.q: What is least count error and how is it reduced?
options: A zero error of the instrument, removed only by recalibration
The error due to the resolution of the instrument, reduced by using an instrument of smaller least count and by averaging repeated readings
An error caused by the observer's reaction time, removed by practice alone
A systematic error that always shifts readings in one fixed direction
mcqs.why: A reading cannot be taken finer than the smallest division the instrument can show, so every reading carries an uncertainty of about one least count; using a finer instrument such as vernier callipers instead of a metre rule, and averaging repeated readings, reduces its effect.

mcqs.q: Why does writing extra calculator digits in an answer not make it more accurate?
options: Because calculators always round the last digit wrongly
Because extra digits shorten the significant figures
Because digits beyond the significant figures are not known reliably and carry no real information about the quantity
Because accuracy depends only on the unit chosen
mcqs.why: The accuracy of a result is limited by the accuracy of the measurements used, not by the number of digits written; digits beyond the significant figures only come from the calculator, are not known reliably, and give a false impression of accuracy.

mcqs.q: What determines the precision of a measurement?
options: The least count, or resolution, of the measuring instrument
The closeness of the measured value to the true value
The number of times the measurement is repeated
The size of the quantity being measured
mcqs.why: Precision is fixed by the position of the last significant digit that can be read, which is set by the least count of the instrument; the smaller the least count, the more precise the measurement can be.

mcqs.q: Two quantities have different dimensions. Which operations are allowed between them?
options: They can be added and subtracted but not multiplied
They can be multiplied and divided, but they cannot be added or subtracted
No operation of any kind is allowed between them
All four operations are always allowed
mcqs.why: Multiplication and division simply combine the dimensions, as length divided by time gives velocity and mass times acceleration gives force, but addition and subtraction mean combining amounts of the same kind, so they require identical dimensions.

mcqs.q: Why are the human pulse and the swing of a pendulum not used as standard units of time?
options: Because both are far too fast to be counted
Because both change and are not invariable or reproducible everywhere, so they cannot serve as reliable standards
Because neither of them repeats regularly at all
Because time can only be measured with atomic standards
mcqs.why: A good unit must be constant, reproducible and the same everywhere; the pulse rate changes with person, health, age and activity, and a pendulum's period changes with its length and with the local value of g, so neither is a reliable standard.

mcqs.q: An equation is found to be dimensionally correct. What can be concluded?
options: The equation is certainly physically correct
The equation must have the correct numerical factors as well
The equation may still be physically wrong, because dimensional analysis cannot detect wrong numerical factors or distinguish quantities with the same dimensions
mcqs.why: Dimensional correctness is necessary but not sufficient: dimensional analysis cannot detect wrong dimensionless factors such as one half or 2 pi, and cannot distinguish different quantities sharing the same dimensions, such as torque and energy, although a dimensionally wrong equation is certainly wrong.

lessons.title: Comprehensive Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Physics is the study of matter, energy and their mutual interactions, covering everything from particles inside the atom to the whole universe.
  • SI has seven base units: metre, kilogram, second, ampere, kelvin, mole and candela; derived units such as the newton are formed from them, and the radian and steradian are the supplementary units.
  • SI unit symbols are not written in plural, take no full stop, and follow the number after a small space, with compound units written using spaces or negative powers.
  • Systematic errors shift results in one direction from known causes and can be removed, while random errors vary unpredictably and are reduced by averaging repeated readings.
  • In addition and subtraction absolute uncertainties add; in multiplication and division percentage uncertainties add; for a power the percentage uncertainty is multiplied by the power.
  • Significant figures are the accurately known digits plus the first doubtful digit, and they show the precision of a measurement.
  • Precision is the degree of exactness fixed by the least count of the instrument, while accuracy is the closeness of a measured value to the true value.
  • Dimensional analysis can check an equation and help derive a formula, but it cannot give dimensionless constants and cannot distinguish torque from energy, which share the same dimensions.

Solved Exercises

Exercise - Comprehensive Questions

Q: Q1. Define Physics? Explain the scope and importance of physics in science, technology and society?

Ans: Physics is the branch of science that deals with the study of matter, energy and their mutual interactions, in specific the physical world and in general the physical universe. Its scope is very wide: it covers everything from the smallest particles inside the atom to the whole universe, and includes mechanics, heat, light, sound, electricity, magnetism and modern topics like nuclear and particle physics. Physics is the foundation of all other sciences and of technology: its laws are used in engineering, medicine (X-rays, lasers, scanners), communication, transport and energy production. In society it has transformed daily life through electricity, electronics, computers and modern transport, so progress in physics directly raises the standard of living.

Q: Q2. What is system of units? In SI what is meant by base, derived and supplementary units?

Ans: A system of units is a complete, organised set of units for measuring all physical quantities, built from a small set of fundamental units. In SI there are seven base units, each for a base quantity, defined independently: metre (length), kilogram (mass), second (time), ampere (current), kelvin (temperature), mole (amount of substance) and candela (luminous intensity). Derived units are formed by multiplying or dividing base units, for example newton = kg m s^-2 for force and joule = kg m^2 s^-2 for energy. Supplementary units are the two dimensionless units for angles: the radian for plane angle and the steradian for solid angle.

Q: Q3. What conventions are used in SI to indicate units?

Ans: The main SI conventions are: unit symbols are written in small letters (m, s, kg), except units named after a person, which begin with a capital letter (N, J, Pa); symbols are never written in plural and no full stop is used after them; the unit is written after the number with a small space, e.g. 43 kg m^-3; compound units are written with a space or negative powers, e.g. m s^-1; prefixes are attached directly to the symbol, e.g. km, ms; and full names of units are written in small letters, e.g. newton, joule, even when named after a person.

Q: Q4. What are errors? Differentiate between systematic and random errors?

Ans: An error is the difference between the measured value and the true value of a quantity; it shows the doubt present in any measurement. Systematic errors always shift the result in one direction, by a fixed amount or proportion, and arise from known causes such as a faulty or zero-error instrument, wrong calibration, or a consistently wrong technique; they can be identified and removed. Random errors vary unpredictably in size and sign from one reading to the next, arising from unknown and uncontrollable causes such as fluctuations in conditions or the observer's judgement; they cannot be removed but their effect is reduced by repeating the measurement and taking the average.

Q: Q5. What is uncertainty in measurement? explain the propagation of uncertainty in addition, subtraction, multiplication and division?

Ans: Uncertainty is the quantification, or magnitude, of the error or doubt in a measurement; a result is written as measured value +- uncertainty. Propagation rules: In addition, the absolute uncertainties of the quantities are added. In subtraction, the absolute uncertainties are still added (uncertainty always increases, never cancels). In multiplication, the percentage (fractional) uncertainties are added, and the product carries that total percentage uncertainty. In division, the percentage uncertainties are likewise added. For a power, the percentage uncertainty is multiplied by the power. The final absolute uncertainty is then obtained from the total percentage uncertainty of the result.

Q: Q6. What are significant figures? What are the rules for determining significant figures in the final result after addition, subtraction, multiplication and division?

Ans: Significant figures are the accurately known digits in a measurement plus the first doubtful digit; they show the precision of the measurement. Counting rules: all non-zero digits are significant; zeros between non-zero digits are significant; leading zeros are not significant; trailing zeros after a decimal point are significant. Rules for results: after addition or subtraction, the result is rounded to the least number of decimal places among the quantities (e.g. 1.513 m + 27.3 m = 28.8 m). After multiplication or division, the result is rounded to the least number of significant figures among the quantities (e.g. 7.635 x 4.81 = 36.7).

Q: Q7. Differentiate between precision and accuracy in the measurement.

Ans: Precision is the degree of exactness with which a measurement is made and stated; it depends on the least count of the instrument and is shown by the position of the last significant digit. Accuracy is the closeness of the measured value to the true (actual) value of the quantity. A measurement can be precise but not accurate, for example repeated readings clustered together but all shifted by a zero error; accuracy is affected by systematic errors, while precision is limited by resolution and random scatter.

Q: Q8. What is meant by dimensions of physical quantities? What are limitations and applications of dimensional analysis?

Ans: The dimensions of a physical quantity are the powers to which the base quantities (mass M, length L, time T, etc.) are raised to express that quantity, e.g. force has dimensions [M L T^-2]. Applications: checking the correctness of an equation by the principle of homogeneity (both sides must have the same dimensions); deriving a possible formula relating quantities, e.g. T = 2 pi sqrt(l / g) apart from the constant; and converting units between systems. Limitations: it gives no information about dimensionless constants such as 2 pi or 1/2; it cannot distinguish quantities having the same dimensions (torque and energy, both [M L^2 T^-2]); and a dimensionally correct equation is not guaranteed to be physically correct.

mcqs.q: Which statement best describes the scope and importance of physics?
options: Physics deals only with moving objects and machines
Physics studies matter, energy and their interactions, from particles inside the atom to the whole universe, and underlies engineering, medicine, communication and transport
Physics is important only inside the laboratory
Physics covers only heat, light and sound
mcqs.why: Physics deals with matter, energy and their mutual interactions across everything from the smallest particles inside the atom to the whole universe, and its laws are used in engineering, medicine such as X-rays and scanners, communication, transport and energy production.

mcqs.q: How many base units are there in SI, and which set lists them correctly?
options: Five: metre, kilogram, second, ampere and kelvin
Nine, including the radian and the steradian
Seven: metre, kilogram, second, ampere, kelvin, mole and candela
Seven: metre, kilogram, second, newton, joule, kelvin and candela
mcqs.why: SI has seven independently defined base units, one for each base quantity: metre for length, kilogram for mass, second for time, ampere for current, kelvin for temperature, mole for amount of substance and candela for luminous intensity.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is a derived SI unit expressed correctly in base units?
options: Newton equals kg m s to the power minus 2
Joule equals kg m s to the power minus 2
Newton equals kg m squared s to the power minus 2
Pascal equals kg m squared s to the power minus 2
mcqs.why: Derived units are formed by multiplying or dividing base units; force is mass times acceleration, so the newton is kilogram times metre per second squared, written kg m s to the power minus 2, while the joule carries an extra metre.

mcqs.q: What are the supplementary units in SI?
options: The radian for plane angle and the steradian for solid angle, both dimensionless
Prefixes such as kilo and milli
mcqs.why: The supplementary units are the two dimensionless angle units: the radian for plane angle and the steradian for solid angle, standing alongside the seven base units and the derived units formed from them.

mcqs.q: Which writing follows the SI conventions for units?
options: 43 kg m to the power minus 3, with a space between the number and the unit and no plural or full stop on the symbol
Newton written in full with a capital N in the middle of a sentence
mcqs.why: SI symbols are written in small letters except those named after a person, are never plural and take no full stop; the unit follows the number after a small space, compound units use spaces or negative powers, and full unit names are written in small letters.

mcqs.q: What is a systematic error?
options: An error that varies unpredictably in size and sign from reading to reading
An error arising from unknown fluctuations that can only be averaged out
An error that always shifts the result in one direction by a fixed amount or proportion, arising from a known cause such as a zero error or wrong calibration, and which can be identified and removed
An error caused only by the least count of the instrument
mcqs.why: Systematic errors come from known causes such as a faulty or zero-error instrument, wrong calibration or a consistently wrong technique; because they always act in one direction they can be identified and removed, unlike random errors.

mcqs.q: What is a random error and how is its effect reduced?
options: An error from a faulty instrument, removed by recalibration
An error that varies unpredictably in size and sign between readings, whose effect is reduced by repeating the measurement and taking the average
An error that is always the same fixed amount
An error that can be removed completely by careful technique
mcqs.why: Random errors arise from unknown and uncontrollable causes such as fluctuations in conditions or the observer's judgement, so they change unpredictably from one reading to the next; they cannot be removed, but repeating the measurement and averaging reduces their effect.

mcqs.q: How do uncertainties propagate in addition and in multiplication?
options: In both cases the percentage uncertainties are added
In addition the absolute uncertainties are added, while in multiplication the percentage uncertainties are added
In addition the percentage uncertainties are added, while in multiplication the absolute uncertainties are added
Uncertainties cancel out in subtraction and stay unchanged in multiplication
mcqs.why: Uncertainty is the magnitude of the doubt in a measurement; for addition and subtraction the absolute uncertainties add, while for multiplication and division the percentage or fractional uncertainties add, and for a power the percentage uncertainty is multiplied by the power.

mcqs.q: A result is calculated as 7.635 multiplied by 4.81. To how many significant figures should it be reported, and why?
options: Five, because the calculator shows five figures
Three, because a multiplication result is rounded to the least number of significant figures among the quantities, which is three in 4.81
Four, because 7.635 has four significant figures
Two, because the result must match the decimal places
mcqs.why: For multiplication and division the result keeps the least number of significant figures of the quantities involved; 4.81 has three and 7.635 has four, so the product 36.72435 is reported to three significant figures as 36.7.

mcqs.q: Which statement correctly distinguishes precision from accuracy?
options: Precision is closeness to the true value, and accuracy is fineness of the reading
They are two names for exactly the same property

Precision is the degree of exactness fixed by the least count, while accuracy is the closeness of the measured value to the true value, so readings can be precise but shifted by a zero error and therefore inaccurate
Accuracy is limited only by random scatter and precision only by systematic errors
mcqs.why: Precision depends on the least count of the instrument and is shown by the position of the last significant digit, whereas accuracy is closeness to the true value; repeated readings can cluster tightly yet all be shifted by a zero error, making them precise but not accurate.

lessons.title: Numerical Problems and Assignments
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • For gears in contact the arc length is shared, so S = r theta for the small gear gives the rotation of the large gear as S divided by its radius.
  • The depth lifted by a pulley equals the number of rotations multiplied by the circumference 2 pi r of the pulley.
  • In subtraction the absolute uncertainties add, so the difference of two wall widths each uncertain by 0.1 cm is uncertain by 0.2 cm.
  • For the volume of a sphere the percentage uncertainty is three times the percentage uncertainty in the radius, because the radius is cubed.
  • The time period of a simple pendulum is T = 2 pi sqrt(l / g) and does not depend on the mass of the bob.
  • The period of a pendulum of length 1.5 m is about 2.5 s with a percentage uncertainty of about 0.8 percent.
  • The area of a 1.50 m by 0.20 m sheet is 0.30 square metres with an uncertainty of about 0.02 square metres.
  • Planck's constant has dimensions M L squared T to the power minus 1 and the gravitational constant has dimensions M to the power minus 1 L cubed T to the power minus 2.

Solved Exercises

Extension Exercise

Q: Q1. What is the angle in degrees through which the larger gear has rotated?

Ans: This refers to Example 1.1 (Gears): the smaller gear of radius r_s = 0.4 m makes one complete rotation, and the larger gear has radius r_L = 0.7 m.
Given: Angle of smaller gear theta_s = 2 pi rad, r_s = 0.4 m, r_L = 0.7 m
Formula: S = r_s x theta_s and theta_L = S / r_L, and 1 rad = 180 / pi degrees = 57.3 degrees
Substitution: S = 0.4 m x 2 pi = 0.8 pi m
theta_L = 0.8 pi m / 0.7 m = 3.6 rad
theta_L in degrees = 3.6 x 57.3 degrees = 206 degrees
Answer: 3.6 rad, i.e. about 206 degrees

Assignment 1.1

Q: Q1. A pulley of radius 0.9 m is used to lift a bucket from the well. If it took 3.6 rotations for the pulley to take water out of the well, how deep is water in the well? (Answer = 20 m)

Ans: Given: Radius of pulley r = 0.9 m, number of rotations n = 3.6
Formula: Depth = n x circumference of pulley = n x 2 pi r
Substitution: Depth = 3.6 x 2 x 3.14 x 0.9 m
Depth = 3.6 x 5.65 m
Depth = 20.4 m
Answer: About 20 m

Assignment 1.2 - Wall Width

Q: Q1. A physicist calculated the wall width of half brick thickness (the brick is laid in a flat position, lengthwise called stretcher position), as (13.6 +- 0.1) cm. And one brick thickness (the brick is placed in flat position, lengthwise orthogonal to wall, called header position), as (23.6 +- 0.1) cm. Calculate the difference in width of walls with uncertainty in it. (10.0 +- 0.2) cm

Ans: Given: One brick thickness = (23.6 +- 0.1) cm, half brick thickness = (13.6 +- 0.1) cm
Formula: In subtraction the absolute uncertainties are added: Difference = (23.6 - 13.6) +- (0.1 + 0.1) cm
Substitution: Difference = 10.0 +- 0.2 cm
Answer: (10.0 +- 0.2) cm

Assignment 1.3 - Resistance

Q: Q1. The voltage 'V (V +- Delta V)' is measured as 7.3 V +- 0.1 V and current 'I (I +- Delta I)' is measured as 2.73 A +- 0.05 A. Calculate the resistance 'R' by using Ohm's Law as R = V / I. (2.7 +- 0.08) ohm

Ans: Given: V = 7.3 V +- 0.1 V, I = 2.73 A +- 0.05 A
Formula: R = V / I; in division percentage uncertainties are added
Substitution: R = 7.3 / 2.73 = 2.67 ohm
Percentage uncertainty in V = (0.1 / 7.3) x 100 = 1.37 percent
Percentage uncertainty in I = (0.05 / 2.73) x 100 = 1.83 percent
Total percentage uncertainty = 1.37 + 1.83 = 3.2 percent
Delta R = 3.2 percent of 2.67 = 0.086 ohm, about 0.08 ohm
Answer: R = (2.7 +- 0.08) ohm

Assignment 1.4 - Volume of Sphere

Q: Q1. The radius of sphere 'r' is measured with vernier callipers as (r +- Delta r) = (2.25 +- 0.01) cm. Calculate the volume of sphere. (47.7 +- 0.6) cm^3

Ans: Given: r = (2.25 +- 0.01) cm
Formula: V = (4/3) pi r^3; for a power, percentage uncertainty is multiplied by the power
Substitution: V = (4/3) x 3.14 x (2.25)^3 = 4.19 x 11.39 = 47.7 cm^3
Percentage uncertainty in r = (0.01 / 2.25) x 100 = 0.44 percent
Percentage uncertainty in V = 3 x 0.44 = 1.33 percent
Delta V = 1.33 percent of 47.7 = 0.64 cm^3, about 0.6 cm^3
Answer: V = (47.7 +- 0.6) cm^3

Assignment 1.5 - Significant Figures Calculation

Q: Q1. Calculate the answers to the appropriate number of significant figures. (a) 0.31 + 0.1 (b) 658.0 + 23.5478 + 1345.29 (c) 8 x 7 (d) 0.9935 x 10.48 x 13.4 (e) 5.5 / 1.1 (f) (73.2 + 18.72 x 6.1) / 3.4. (a) 0.4, (b) 2026.8, (c) 60 (d) 140 or 1.40 x 10^2, (e) 5.0 and (f) 55

Ans: For addition and subtraction the result is rounded to the least number of decimal places; for multiplication and division it is rounded to the least number of significant figures.
(a) 0.31 + 0.1 = 0.41, rounded to one decimal place = 0.4
(b) 658.0 + 23.5478 + 1345.29 = 2026.8378, rounded to one decimal place (658.0) = 2026.8
(c) 8 x 7 = 56, both factors have one significant figure, so = 60 (one significant figure)
(d) 0.9935 x 10.48 x 13.4 = 139.5, least significant figures = 3 (13.4), so = 140 or 1.40 x 10^2
(e) 5.5 / 1.1 = 5.0 (two significant figures)
(f) First 18.72 x 6.1 = 114.2; then 73.2 + 114.2 = 187.4; then 187.4 / 3.4 = 55.1, rounded to two significant figures = 55
Answer: (a) 0.4, (b) 2026.8, (c) 60, (d) 140, (e) 5.0, (f) 55

Assignment 1.6 - Formula for Time Period

Q: Q1. Show that the equations (a) v_f = v_i + a t (b) S = v_i t + (1/2) a t^2 are dimensionally correct.

Ans: A dimensionally correct equation has the same dimensions on both sides. Dimensions: velocity [L T^-1], acceleration [L T^-2], time [T], displacement [L]. The number 1/2 is dimensionless.
(a) Left side: [v_f] = [L T^-1]. Right side: [v_i] = [L T^-1] and [a t] = [L T^-2] x [T] = [L T^-1]. Both terms on the right have the dimensions of the left side, so v_f = v_i + a t is dimensionally correct.
(b) Left side: [S] = [L]. Right side: [v_i t] = [L T^-1] x [T] = [L] and [(1/2) a t^2] = [L T^-2] x [T^2] = [L]. Both terms have the dimensions of displacement, so S = v_i t + (1/2) a t^2 is dimensionally correct.

Assignment 1.7 - Formula for Time Period

Q: Q1. Find an expression for the time period 'T' of a simple pendulum. The time period 'T' may depend upon (i) mass 'm' of the bob of the pendulum, (ii) length 'l' of pendulum, (iii) acceleration due to gravity 'g' at the place where the pendulum is suspended. T = 2 pi sqrt(l / g)

Ans: Given: Suppose T depends on m, l and g as T = k m^a l^b g^c, where k is a dimensionless constant
Formula: Dimensions: [T] = [T], [m] = [M], [l] = [L], [g] = [L T^-2]
Substitution: [T] = [M]^a [L]^b [L T^-2]^c = [M]^a [L]^(b + c) [T]^(-2c)
Comparing powers: for M: a = 0; for T: -2c = 1, so c = -1/2; for L: b + c = 0, so b = 1/2
Putting a, b and c back: T = k l^(1/2) g^(-1/2) = k sqrt(l / g)
Dimensional analysis cannot give k; experiment gives k = 2 pi
Answer: T = 2 pi sqrt(l / g). The time period does not depend on the mass of the bob.

Exercise - Numerical Questions

Q: Q1. A circular pizza into 3 equal parts, one piece of pizza is taken out. Estimate the degree measure of the single piece of pizza and convert the measure into radians. What is the radian measure of the angle of the remaining part of pizza? (4 pi/3 rad = 4.19 rad and 2 pi/3 rad = 2.09 rad)

Ans: Given: Full circle = 360 degrees = 2 pi rad, divided into 3 equal parts
Formula: Angle of one part = 360 degrees / 3; radians = degrees x (pi / 180)
Substitution: Angle of single piece = 360 / 3 = 120 degrees
In radians = 120 x pi / 180 = 2 pi / 3 rad = 2.09 rad
Angle of remaining part = 360 - 120 = 240 degrees
In radians = 240 x pi / 180 = 4 pi / 3 rad = 4.19 rad
Answer: Single piece = 120 degrees = 2.09 rad; remaining part = 240 degrees = 4.19 rad

Q: Q2. The length of a pendulum is (1.5 +- 0.01) m and the acceleration due to gravity is taken into account as (9.8 +- 0.1) m s^-2. Calculate the time period of the pendulum with uncertainty in it. (2.5 s +- 0.8%)

Ans: Given: l = (1.5 +- 0.01) m, g = (9.8 +- 0.1) m s^-2
Formula: T = 2 pi sqrt(l / g); percentage uncertainty in T = (1/2) x (percentage uncertainty in l + percentage uncertainty in g)
Substitution: T = 2 x 3.14 x sqrt(1.5 / 9.8) = 6.28 x sqrt(0.153) = 6.28 x 0.391 = 2.46 s, about 2.5 s
Percentage uncertainty in l = (0.01 / 1.5) x 100 = 0.67 percent
Percentage uncertainty in g = (0.1 / 9.8) x 100 = 1.02 percent
Percentage uncertainty in T = (1/2) x (0.67 + 1.02) = 0.84 percent, about 0.8 percent
Answer: T = 2.5 s +- 0.8 percent (absolute uncertainty about 0.02 s)

Q: Q3. Determine the area of a rectangular sheet with length (l +- Delta l) = (1.50 +- 0.02) m and width (w +- Delta w) = (0.20 +- 0.01) m. Calculate the area (A +- Delta A). (0.30 m^2, +- 0.02 m^2)

Ans: Given: l = (1.50 +- 0.02) m, w = (0.20 +- 0.01) m
Formula: A = l x w; in multiplication percentage uncertainties are added
Substitution: A = 1.50 x 0.20 = 0.30 m^2
Percentage uncertainty in l = (0.02 / 1.50) x 100 = 1.33 percent
Percentage uncertainty in w = (0.01 / 0.20) x 100 = 5.0 percent
Total percentage uncertainty = 1.33 + 5.0 = 6.33 percent
Delta A = 6.33 percent of 0.30 = 0.019 m^2, about 0.02 m^2
Answer: A = (0.30 +- 0.02) m^2

Q: Q4. Calculate the answer up to appropriate numbers of significant digits (a) 246.24 + 238.278 + 98.3 (b) 1.4 x 2.639 + 117.25 (c) (2.66 x 10^4) - (1.03 x 10^3) (d) (112 x 0.456) / (3.2 x 120) (e) 168.99 x 9 (f) 1023 + 8.5489. (a) 582.8, (b) 120.9, (c) 2.56 x 10^4, (d) 0.13, (e) 2000 and (f) 1032

Ans: Addition and subtraction: round to the least decimal places. Multiplication and division: round to the least significant figures.
(a) 246.24 + 238.278 + 98.3 = 582.818; 98.3 has one decimal place, so answer = 582.8
(b) 1.4 x 2.639 = 3.695; 3.695 + 117.25 = 120.945; limited by 1.4 (two significant figures, tenths place in the product), so answer = 120.9
(c) (2.66 x 10^4) - (1.03 x 10^3) = 26600 - 1030 = 25570 = 2.56 x 10^4 (three significant figures)
(d) (112 x 0.456) / (3.2 x 120) = 51.072 / 384 = 0.133; least significant figures = 2 (3.2), so answer = 0.13
(e) 168.99 x 9 = 1520.91; the factor 9 has one significant figure, so answer = 2000 (one significant figure)
(f) 1023 + 8.5489 = 1031.5489; 1023 has no decimal place, so answer = 1032
Answer: (a) 582.8, (b) 120.9, (c) 2.56 x 10^4, (d) 0.13, (e) 2000, (f) 1032

Q: Q5. Calculate the answer up to appropriate numbers of significant digits (a) The ratio of mass of proton 'm_p' to the mass of electron 'm_e': m_p / m_e = 1.67 x 10^-27 kg / 9.1096 x 10^-31 kg (b) The ratio of charge on electron 'q_e' to mass of electron 'm_e': q_e / m_e = 1.6 x 10^-19 C / 9.1096 x 10^-31 kg. (a) 1.83 x 10^3 and (b) 1.8 x 10^11 C/kg

Ans: In division the result keeps the least number of significant figures of the quantities involved.
(a) Given: m_p = 1.67 x 10^-27 kg (3 significant figures), m_e = 9.1096 x 10^-31 kg
Formula: m_p / m_e = (1.67 x 10^-27) / (9.1096 x 10^-31)
Substitution: = 0.1833 x 10^4 = 1833, rounded to 3 significant figures
Answer (a): 1.83 x 10^3 (dimensionless ratio)
(b) Given: q_e = 1.6 x 10^-19 C (2 significant figures), m_e = 9.1096 x 10^-31 kg
Formula: q_e / m_e = (1.6 x 10^-19) / (9.1096 x 10^-31)
Substitution: = 0.176 x 10^12 = 1.76 x 10^11, rounded to 2 significant figures
Answer (b): 1.8 x 10^11 C/kg

Q: Q6. Find the dimensions of (a) planck's constant 'h' from formula E = h f Where E is the energy and f is frequency. (b) gravitational constant 'G' from the formula F = G m_1 m_2 / r^2 Where 'F' is force, 'm_1' and 'm_2' are masses of objects and 'r' is the distance between centers of objects. (a) [M^1 L^2 T^-1] and (b) [M^-1 L^3 T^-2]

Ans: (a) Given: E = h f, so h = E / f
Formula: [E] = [M L^2 T^-2], [f] = [T^-1]
Substitution: [h] = [M L^2 T^-2] / [T^-1] = [M L^2 T^-1]
Answer (a): Dimensions of h are [M^1 L^2 T^-1]
(b) Given: F = G m_1 m_2 / r^2, so G = F r^2 / (m_1 m_2)
Formula: [F] = [M L T^-2], [r^2] = [L^2], [m_1 m_2] = [M^2]
Substitution: [G] = [M L T^-2] x [L^2] / [M^2] = [M^-1 L^3 T^-2]
Answer (b): Dimensions of G are [M^-1 L^3 T^-2]

Q: Q7. Show that (a) KE = (1/2) m v^2 and (b) PE_g = m g h are dimensionally correct.

Ans: Dimensions needed: [m] = [M], [v] = [L T^-1], [g] = [L T^-2], [h] = [L], energy = [M L^2 T^-2]. The factor 1/2 is dimensionless.
(a) Left side: [KE] = [M L^2 T^-2]
Right side: [(1/2) m v^2] = [M] x [L T^-1]^2 = [M] x [L^2 T^-2] = [M L^2 T^-2]
Both sides are equal, so KE = (1/2) m v^2 is dimensionally correct.
(b) Left side: [PE_g] = [M L^2 T^-2]
Right side: [m g h] = [M] x [L T^-2] x [L] = [M L^2 T^-2]
Both sides are equal, so PE_g = m g h is dimensionally correct.

mcqs.q: What is the angle in degrees through which the larger gear has rotated? The smaller gear of radius 0.4 m makes one complete rotation and the larger gear has radius 0.7 m.
mcqs.why: Formula: S = r_s x theta_s and theta_L = S / r_L, with 1 rad = 57.3 degrees. Substitution: S = 0.4 m x 2 pi = 0.8 pi m, about 2.51 m. Step: theta_L = 2.51 m / 0.7 m = 3.6 rad, and 3.6 x 57.3 = 206 degrees. Result: The larger gear turns through 3.6 rad, about 206 degrees.

mcqs.q: A pulley of radius 0.9 m is used to lift a bucket from the well. If it took 3.6 rotations for the pulley to take water out of the well, how deep is water in the well?
mcqs.why: Formula: Depth = n x circumference = n x 2 pi r. Substitution: Depth = 3.6 x 2 x 3.14 x 0.9 m. Step: 2 x 3.14 x 0.9 = 5.65 m per rotation, and 3.6 x 5.65 = 20.4 m. Result: The water is about 20.4 m, roughly 20 m, below the pulley.

mcqs.q: A physicist calculated the wall width of half brick thickness as (13.6 +- 0.1) cm and one brick thickness as (23.6 +- 0.1) cm. Calculate the difference in width of walls with uncertainty in it.
mcqs.why: Formula: In subtraction the absolute uncertainties are added: Difference = (23.6 - 13.6) +- (0.1 + 0.1) cm. Substitution: 23.6 - 13.6 = 10.0 cm and 0.1 + 0.1 = 0.2 cm. Step: The uncertainty grows rather than cancelling, because each reading may err in either direction. Result: The difference is (10.0 +- 0.2) cm.

mcqs.q: The voltage is measured as 7.3 V +- 0.1 V and current as 2.73 A +- 0.05 A. Calculate the resistance by using Ohm's Law R = V / I.
mcqs.why: Formula: R = V / I, and in division percentage uncertainties are added. Substitution: R = 7.3 / 2.73 = 2.67 ohm; percentage uncertainty in V is 0.1/7.3 x 100 = 1.37 percent and in I is 0.05/2.73 x 100 = 1.83 percent. Step: Total is 3.2 percent, and 3.2 percent of 2.67 is 0.086 ohm, about 0.08 ohm. Result: R = (2.7 +- 0.08) ohm.

mcqs.q: The radius of a sphere is measured with vernier callipers as (2.25 +- 0.01) cm. Calculate the volume of the sphere.
mcqs.why: Formula: V = (4/3) pi r^3, and for a power the percentage uncertainty is multiplied by the power. Substitution: V = 4.19 x (2.25)^3 = 4.19 x 11.39 = 47.7 cm^3; percentage uncertainty in r is 0.01/2.25 x 100 = 0.44 percent. Step: Percentage uncertainty in V is 3 x 0.44 = 1.33 percent, and 1.33 percent of 47.7 is 0.64 cm^3, about 0.6 cm^3. Result: V = (47.7 +- 0.6) cm^3.

mcqs.q: Calculate the answers to the appropriate number of significant figures: (a) 0.31 + 0.1 (b) 658.0 + 23.5478 + 1345.29 (c) 8 x 7 (d) 0.9935 x 10.48 x 13.4 (e) 5.5 / 1.1 (f) (73.2 + 18.72 x 6.1) / 3.4
mcqs.why: Formula: Additions and subtractions round to the least decimal places; multiplications and divisions round to the least significant figures. Substitution: (a) 0.41 rounds to 0.4; (b) 2026.8378 rounds to 2026.8; (c) 56 with one significant figure becomes 60; (d) 139.5 with three significant figures becomes 140; (e) 5.5/1.1 = 5.0; (f) (73.2 + 114.2)/3.4 = 55.1, rounded to 55. Step: Each part is rounded only at the end, using the rule for the operation performed last. Result: (a) 0.4, (b) 2026.8, (c) 60, (d) 140, (e) 5.0, (f) 55.

mcqs.q: Show that the equations (a) v_f = v_i + a t (b) S = v_i t + (1/2) a t^2 are dimensionally correct. What is the correct conclusion?
options: Only the first equation is dimensionally correct
Only the second equation is dimensionally correct
mcqs.why: Formula: Dimensions are [v] = [L T^-1], [a] = [L T^-2], [t] = [T] and [S] = [L], while 1/2 is dimensionless. Substitution: For the first equation [a t] = [L T^-2] x [T] = [L T^-1], matching [v_f] and [v_i]; for the second, [v_i t] = [L] and [(1/2) a t^2] = [L T^-2] x [T^2] = [L], matching [S]. Step: Every term on each side carries the same dimensions, satisfying the principle of homogeneity. Result: Both equations are dimensionally correct.

mcqs.q: Find an expression for the time period T of a simple pendulum, which may depend on the mass m of the bob, the length l of the pendulum and the acceleration due to gravity g.
options: T = 2 pi sqrt(l / g), independent of the mass of the bob
mcqs.why: Formula: Assume T = k m^a l^b g^c with k dimensionless, using [T] = [T], [m] = [M], [l] = [L] and [g] = [L T^-2]. Substitution: [T] = [M]^a [L]^(b+c) [T]^(-2c). Step: Comparing powers gives a = 0 for mass, -2c = 1 so c = -1/2 for time, and b + c = 0 so b = 1/2 for length, giving T = k sqrt(l / g); experiment fixes k = 2 pi. Result: T = 2 pi sqrt(l / g), and the period does not depend on the mass of the bob.

mcqs.q: A circular pizza is cut into 3 equal parts and one piece is taken out. What are the degree and radian measures of the single piece and of the remaining part?
options: Single piece 120 degrees = 2.09 rad; remaining part 240 degrees = 4.19 rad
Single piece 90 degrees = 1.57 rad; remaining part 270 degrees = 4.71 rad
Single piece 120 degrees = 4.19 rad; remaining part 240 degrees = 2.09 rad
Single piece 60 degrees = 1.05 rad; remaining part 300 degrees = 5.24 rad
mcqs.why: Formula: Angle of one part = 360 degrees / 3, and radians = degrees x (pi / 180). Substitution: One part is 360 / 3 = 120 degrees, which is 120 x pi / 180 = 2 pi / 3 = 2.09 rad. Step: The remaining part is 360 - 120 = 240 degrees, which is 240 x pi / 180 = 4 pi / 3 = 4.19 rad. Result: Single piece 120 degrees = 2.09 rad; remaining part 240 degrees = 4.19 rad.

mcqs.q: The length of a pendulum is (1.5 +- 0.01) m and g is (9.8 +- 0.1) m s^-2. Calculate the time period of the pendulum with uncertainty in it.
mcqs.why: Formula: T = 2 pi sqrt(l / g), and the percentage uncertainty in T is one half of the sum of the percentage uncertainties in l and g because of the square root. Substitution: T = 6.28 x sqrt(1.5 / 9.8) = 6.28 x 0.391 = 2.46 s, about 2.5 s; percentage uncertainty in l is 0.67 percent and in g is 1.02 percent. Step: Half of (0.67 + 1.02) is 0.84 percent, about 0.8 percent. Result: T = 2.5 s +- 0.8 percent.

mcqs.q: Determine the area of a rectangular sheet with length (1.50 +- 0.02) m and width (0.20 +- 0.01) m.
mcqs.why: Formula: A = l x w, and in multiplication the percentage uncertainties are added. Substitution: A = 1.50 x 0.20 = 0.30 m^2; percentage uncertainty in l is 0.02/1.50 x 100 = 1.33 percent and in w is 0.01/0.20 x 100 = 5.0 percent. Step: Total percentage uncertainty is 6.33 percent, and 6.33 percent of 0.30 is 0.019 m^2, about 0.02 m^2. Result: A = (0.30 +- 0.02) m^2.

mcqs.q: Calculate the answer up to appropriate numbers of significant digits: (a) 246.24 + 238.278 + 98.3 (b) 1.4 x 2.639 + 117.25 (c) (2.66 x 10^4) - (1.03 x 10^3) (d) (112 x 0.456) / (3.2 x 120) (e) 168.99 x 9 (f) 1023 + 8.5489
mcqs.why: Formula: Additions round to the least decimal places and multiplications or divisions to the least significant figures. Substitution: (a) 582.818 rounds to 582.8; (b) 3.695 + 117.25 = 120.945, reported as 120.9; (c) 26600 - 1030 = 25570 = 2.56 x 10^4; (d) 51.072 / 384 = 0.133, reported to two significant figures as 0.13; (e) 1520.91 with one significant figure becomes 2000; (f) 1031.5489 rounds to 1032. Step: The limiting quantity in each part decides the final rounding. Result: (a) 582.8, (b) 120.9, (c) 2.56 x 10^4, (d) 0.13, (e) 2000, (f) 1032.

mcqs.q: Calculate up to appropriate significant digits: (a) the ratio of the mass of a proton to the mass of an electron, 1.67 x 10^-27 kg / 9.1096 x 10^-31 kg (b) the ratio of the charge on an electron to its mass, 1.6 x 10^-19 C / 9.1096 x 10^-31 kg
mcqs.why: Formula: In division the result keeps the least number of significant figures of the quantities involved. Substitution: (a) (1.67 x 10^-27) / (9.1096 x 10^-31) = 0.1833 x 10^4 = 1833, rounded to three significant figures; (b) (1.6 x 10^-19) / (9.1096 x 10^-31) = 0.176 x 10^12 = 1.76 x 10^11, rounded to two significant figures. Step: The proton mass has three significant figures and the electron charge has two, fixing each rounding. Result: (a) 1.83 x 10^3 and (b) 1.8 x 10^11 C/kg.

mcqs.q: Find the dimensions of (a) Planck's constant h from E = h f and (b) the gravitational constant G from F = G m_1 m_2 / r^2.
mcqs.why: Formula: h = E / f with [E] = [M L^2 T^-2] and [f] = [T^-1]; G = F r^2 / (m_1 m_2) with [F] = [M L T^-2], [r^2] = [L^2] and [m_1 m_2] = [M^2]. Substitution: [h] = [M L^2 T^-2] / [T^-1] = [M L^2 T^-1]; [G] = [M L T^-2] x [L^2] / [M^2] = [M^-1 L^3 T^-2]. Step: Powers of each base quantity are added on multiplication and subtracted on division. Result: (a) [M L^2 T^-1] and (b) [M^-1 L^3 T^-2].

mcqs.q: Show that (a) KE = (1/2) m v^2 and (b) PE_g = m g h are dimensionally correct. What is the correct conclusion?
options: Only the kinetic energy equation is dimensionally correct
Only the potential energy equation is dimensionally correct
mcqs.why: Formula: Energy has dimensions [M L^2 T^-2], with [m] = [M], [v] = [L T^-1], [g] = [L T^-2] and [h] = [L], while 1/2 is dimensionless. Substitution: [(1/2) m v^2] = [M] x [L^2 T^-2] = [M L^2 T^-2]; [m g h] = [M] x [L T^-2] x [L] = [M L^2 T^-2]. Step: In each case the right side matches the dimensions of energy on the left side. Result: Both equations are dimensionally correct.

lessons.title: Multiple Choice Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Three vectors of unequal magnitude is the minimum number that can be arranged to give a zero resultant.
  • The resultant of two vectors of magnitude A is also A only when the angle between them is 120 degrees.
  • The magnitude of the vector 2 i + j + 2 k is 3, from the square root of the sum of its squared components.
  • The resultant of two forces must lie between the difference and the sum of their magnitudes, so 20 N and 50 N can never give a 20 N resultant.
  • When the dot product of two nonzero vectors is zero they are perpendicular, and the magnitude of their cross product is then A B.
  • The scalar triple product A . (A x B) is always zero because A cross B is perpendicular to A.
  • The magnitudes of the dot and cross products are equal when the angle between the vectors is 45 degrees.
  • Torque is force multiplied by the moment arm, so opposing tangential forces on a wheel give a net torque equal to the difference of their individual torques.

Solved Exercises

Exercise - Multiple Choice Questions

Q: Q1. Two vectors lie with their tails at the same point. When the angle between them is increased by 20 degrees their scalar product has the same magnitude but changes from positive to negative. The original angle between them was:

Options: (a) 0 (b) 60 degrees (c) 70 degrees (d) 80 degrees

Correct answer: 80 degrees

Q: Q2. The minimum number of vectors of unequal magnitude required to produce a zero resultant is

Options: (a) 2 (b) 3 (c) 4 (d) 5

Correct answer: 3

Q: Q3. If the resultant of two vectors, each of magnitude A is also a magnitude of A. the angle between the two vectors will be:

Options: (a) 30 degrees (b) 45 degrees (c) 60 degrees (d) 120 degrees

Correct answer: 120 degrees

Q: Q4. The magnitude of vector A = 2 i + j + 2 k is

Options: (a) 9 (b) 5 (c) 3 (d) 1

Correct answer: 3

Q: Q5. When F_x = 3 N and F = 5 N then F_y =

Options: (a) 6 N (b) 4 N (c) 2 N (d) 0 N

Correct answer: 4 N

Q: Q6. A meter stick is supported by a knife-edge at the 50-cm mark. Arif hangs masses of 0.40 kg and 0.60 kg from the 20-cm and 80-cm marks, respectively. Where should Arif hang a third mass of 0.30 kg to keep the stick balanced?

Options: (a) 20 cm (b) 70 cm (c) 30 cm (d) 25 cm

Correct answer: 30 cm

Q: Q7. If A_x = 1.5 cm, A_y = -1.0 cm, into which quadrant do the vector A point?

Options: (a) I (b) II (c) III (d) IV

Correct answer: IV

Q: Q8. A . (A x B) = ?

Options: (a) 0 (b) 1 (c) A B (d) A^2 B

Correct answer: 0

Q: Q9. Two forces of magnitude 20 N and 50 N act simultaneously on a body. Which one of the following forces cannot be a resultant of the two forces?

Options: (a) 20 N (b) 30 N (c) 40 N (d) 70 N

Correct answer: 20 N

Q: Q10. If the dot product of two nonzero vectors A and B is zero then the magnitude of their cross product is __

Options: (a) 0 (b) 1 (c) A B (d) -A B

Correct answer: A B

Q: Q11. The sum of magnitudes of two forces is 16 N. If the resultant force is 8 N and its direction is perpendicular to minimum force then the forces are

Options: (a) 6 N and 10 N (b) 8 N and 8 N (c) 4 N and 12 N (d) 2 N and 14 N

Correct answer: 6 N and 10 N

Q: Q12. Find the mass of the uneven rod shown in the figure. If its center of gravity is 14 cm from end A is ____. Diagram (in words): A horizontal uneven rod, thick and rounded at the left end labelled End A and tapering to a point at the right; a red downward arrow labelled m = ? marks the centre of gravity, 14 cm from end A; the rod rests on a triangular pivot (fulcrum) 30 cm from end A; a weight labelled 80 g hangs at the pointed end, 20 cm to the right of the pivot.

Options: (a) 100 g (b) 150 g (c) 80 g (d) 5 g

Correct answer: 100 g

Q: Q13. The following diagrams show a uniform rod with its midpoint on the pivot. Two equal forces F are applied on the rod, as shown in the Figure. Which diagram shows the rod in equilibrium?

Options: (a) A: rod with force F downward at the left end and force F upward at the right end, pivot at the midpoint (b) B: rod with force F upward at the left end and force F upward just right of the central pivot (c) C: rod with force F downward at the left end and force F downward at the right end, pivot at the midpoint (d) D: rod with force F upward on the left half and force F downward at the right end, pivot at the midpoint

Correct answer: C: rod with force F downward at the left end and force F downward at the right end, pivot at the midpoint

Q: Q14. For which angle the equation |A . B| = |A x B| is correct.

Options: (a) 30 degrees (b) 45 degrees (c) 60 degrees (d) 90 degrees

Correct answer: 45 degrees

Q: Q15. What is the net torque on wheel radius 2 m as shown? Diagram (in words): A circular wheel of radius 2 m with a horizontal diameter line drawn across its centre; at the leftmost point of the rim a green upward arrow labelled 10 N points up; at the rightmost point of the rim an orange upward arrow labelled 5 N points up. Both forces are tangent to the wheel.

Options: (a) 10 N anticlockwise (b) 10 N m anticlockwise (c) 10 N m clockwise (d) 5 N m clockwise

Correct answer: 10 N m clockwise

mcqs.q: Two vectors lie with their tails at the same point. When the angle between them is increased by 20 degrees their scalar product has the same magnitude but changes from positive to negative. The original angle between them was:
mcqs.why: Let the original angle be theta; increasing it by 20 degrees makes the cosine change sign with the same magnitude, so cos theta equals minus cos(theta + 20 degrees), which gives theta + (theta + 20) = 180 degrees and theta = 80 degrees.

mcqs.q: The minimum number of vectors of unequal magnitude required to produce a zero resultant is
mcqs.why: Two vectors of unequal magnitude can at best partly cancel and can never give a zero resultant, while three vectors can be arranged head to tail as a closed triangle, so the minimum number required is three.

mcqs.q: If the resultant of two vectors, each of magnitude A is also a magnitude of A. the angle between the two vectors will be:
mcqs.why: With R squared equal to A squared plus A squared plus 2 A squared cos theta, setting R equal to A gives cos theta equal to minus one half, so the angle between the two equal vectors is 120 degrees.

mcqs.q: The magnitude of vector A = 2 i + j + 2 k is
mcqs.why: The magnitude is the square root of the sum of the squared components: the square root of 4 plus 1 plus 4 is the square root of 9, which is 3.

mcqs.q: When F_x = 3 N and F = 5 N then F_y =
mcqs.why: The components satisfy F squared equal to F_x squared plus F_y squared, so F_y squared is 25 minus 9, which is 16, giving F_y equal to 4 N.

mcqs.q: A meter stick is supported by a knife-edge at the 50-cm mark. Arif hangs masses of 0.40 kg and 0.60 kg from the 20-cm and 80-cm marks, respectively. Where should Arif hang a third mass of 0.30 kg to keep the stick balanced?
mcqs.why: Torques about the 50 cm pivot must balance: the 0.40 kg mass gives 0.40 x 30 on the left and the 0.60 kg mass gives 0.60 x 30 on the right, so the 0.30 kg mass must supply 6 units of torque on the left, 20 cm from the pivot, which is the 30 cm mark.

mcqs.q: If A_x = 1.5 cm, A_y = -1.0 cm, into which quadrant do the vector A point?
mcqs.why: A positive x component and a negative y component place the tip of the vector below the positive x-axis and to its right, which is the fourth quadrant.

mcqs.q: A . (A x B) = ?
mcqs.why: The cross product A cross B is perpendicular to the plane of A and B and therefore perpendicular to A itself, so its scalar product with A is always zero.

mcqs.q: Two forces of magnitude 20 N and 50 N act simultaneously on a body. Which one of the following forces cannot be a resultant of the two forces?
mcqs.why: The resultant of 20 N and 50 N must lie between 50 minus 20 and 50 plus 20, that is between 30 N and 70 N, so a resultant of 20 N is impossible.

mcqs.q: If the dot product of two nonzero vectors A and B is zero then the magnitude of their cross product is __
mcqs.why: A zero dot product means cos theta is zero, so the vectors are perpendicular and sin theta is one, making the magnitude of their cross product equal to A B.

mcqs.q: The sum of magnitudes of two forces is 16 N. If the resultant force is 8 N and its direction is perpendicular to minimum force then the forces are
mcqs.why: With the resultant perpendicular to the smaller force, the larger force is the hypotenuse: 10 squared equals 8 squared plus 6 squared, and the two magnitudes add to 16 N, giving forces of 6 N and 10 N.

mcqs.q: Find the mass of the uneven rod shown in the figure. If its center of gravity is 14 cm from end A is ____. Diagram (in words): A horizontal uneven rod, thick and rounded at the left end labelled End A and tapering to a point at the right; a red downward arrow labelled m = ? marks the centre of gravity, 14 cm from end A; the rod rests on a triangular pivot (fulcrum) 30 cm from end A; a weight labelled 80 g hangs at the pointed end, 20 cm to the right of the pivot.
mcqs.why: Taking torques about the pivot 30 cm from end A: the rod's weight acts at its centre of gravity 16 cm to the left of the pivot, so m x 16 = 80 x 20, giving m = 100 g.

mcqs.q: The following diagrams show a uniform rod with its midpoint on the pivot. Two equal forces F are applied on the rod, as shown in the Figure. Which diagram shows the rod in equilibrium?
options: A: rod with force F downward at the left end and force F upward at the right end, pivot at the midpoint
B: rod with force F upward at the left end and force F upward just right of the central pivot
C: rod with force F downward at the left end and force F downward at the right end, pivot at the midpoint
D: rod with force F upward on the left half and force F downward at the right end, pivot at the midpoint
mcqs.why: In the arrangement with equal downward forces at both ends, the two torques about the central pivot are equal and opposite and cancel, while the pivot itself supplies the upward force that balances the total downward force, so the rod stays in equilibrium.

mcqs.q: For which angle the equation |A . B| = |A x B| is correct.
mcqs.why: Equality of the magnitudes means A B cos theta equals A B sin theta, so tan theta equals one, which gives an angle of 45 degrees between the vectors.

mcqs.q: What is the net torque on wheel radius 2 m as shown? Diagram (in words): A circular wheel of radius 2 m with a horizontal diameter line drawn across its centre; at the leftmost point of the rim a green upward arrow labelled 10 N points up; at the rightmost point of the rim an orange upward arrow labelled 5 N points up. Both forces are tangent to the wheel.
mcqs.why: The 10 N force at the left rim gives a torque of 10 x 2 = 20 N m clockwise, while the 5 N force at the right rim gives 5 x 2 = 10 N m anticlockwise, leaving a net torque of 10 N m clockwise.

lessons.title: Conceptual Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Three vectors of equal magnitude placed head to tail at 120 degrees to each other form a closed triangle and add to a null vector.
  • Vectors of 2 m, 3 m and 5 m can add to zero only when collinear, with the 2 m and 3 m vectors together opposing the 5 m vector.
  • The unit vectors i, j and k are dimensionless, have magnitude 1 and only specify direction; the components carry the units of the quantity.
  • The scalar product of two vectors is negative when the angle between them is greater than 90 degrees, as in the work done by friction.
  • The scalar product of two nonzero vectors is zero when they are perpendicular, and the vector product is zero when they are parallel or antiparallel.
  • If both the scalar and vector products of a nonzero vector A with a vector B are zero, then B must be the zero vector.
  • A particle under a single force cannot be in equilibrium, because that force is the unbalanced net force and produces acceleration.
  • A central force produces no torque about its fixed point, because the position vector and the force are parallel and sin theta is zero.

Solved Exercises

Exercise - Conceptual Questions

Q: Q1. Is it possible to add three vectors of equal magnitude but different directions to get a null vector? Illustrate with a diagram.

Ans: Diagram (in words): Three arrows of equal length placed head to tail at 120 degrees to each other, forming a closed equilateral triangle and returning to the starting point.
Yes, it is possible. If three vectors of equal magnitude are arranged head to tail with 120 degrees between consecutive directions, they form a closed equilateral triangle. The head of the last vector meets the tail of the first, so their vector sum is the null (zero) vector. In components, the horizontal and vertical components cancel in pairs, confirming the resultant is zero.

Q: Q2. The magnitudes of three vectors are 2 m, 3 m, and 5 m, respectively. The directions are at your disposal. Can these three vectors be added to yield zero? Illustrate with a diagram.

Ans: Diagram (in words): The 2 m and 3 m vectors placed along the same line in the same direction give a combined 5 m vector; the 5 m vector placed exactly opposite to them closes the line back to the starting point.
Yes, these can add to zero, but only in one special arrangement: the 2 m and 5 m condition is met when the 2 m and 3 m vectors point in exactly the same direction and the 5 m vector points exactly opposite to them, so 2 + 3 - 5 = 0. They cannot form a triangle, because 2 + 3 = 5 exactly, so the three vectors must be collinear; in any other arrangement the sum is not zero.

Q: Q3. What units are associated with the unit vectors i, j, and k?

Ans: The unit vectors i, j and k themselves are dimensionless: they have magnitude 1 and only specify direction along the x, y and z axes respectively, so no units are associated with the unit vectors themselves. The components written with them carry the units of the vector quantity being represented; for example, in a displacement A = A_x i + A_y j + A_z k, A_x, A_y and A_z are in metres, and in a force they are in newtons.

Q: Q4. Can a scalar product of two vectors be negative? Provide a proof and give an example.

Ans: Yes. The scalar product is A . B = A B cos theta. When the angle theta between the vectors is greater than 90 degrees and less than 180 degrees, cos theta is negative, so the product is negative. Proof: for theta = 120 degrees, cos 120 degrees = -1/2, giving A . B = -A B / 2, a negative value. Example: the work done by friction is negative because the friction force acts opposite (180 degrees) to the displacement; another example is A = i and B = -i, whose dot product is -1.

Q: Q5. A and B are two nonzero vectors. How can their scalar product be zero? And how can their vector product be zero?

Ans: For nonzero vectors A and B: the scalar product A . B = A B cos theta is zero when cos theta = 0, that is when theta = 90 degrees, so the vectors are perpendicular to each other. The vector product has magnitude A B sin theta, which is zero when sin theta = 0, that is when theta = 0 degrees or 180 degrees, so the vectors are parallel or antiparallel (collinear).

Q: Q6. Suppose you are given a known nonzero vector A. The scalar product of A with an unknown vector B is zero. Likewise, the vector product of A with B is zero. What can you conclude about B?

Ans: A . B = 0 means either B = 0 or B is perpendicular to A. A cross B = 0 means either B = 0 or B is parallel to A. A nonzero B cannot be both perpendicular and parallel to the nonzero vector A at the same time, so the only possibility satisfying both conditions together is that B is the zero vector: B = 0.

Q: Q7. Why a particle experiencing only one force cannot be in equilibrium?

Ans: Equilibrium of a particle requires the net force on it to be zero (first condition of equilibrium, sum of F = 0), so that it has no acceleration. A single force acting on a particle is itself the net force and is nonzero; there is no other force to cancel it, so the particle must accelerate in the direction of that force and cannot be in equilibrium.

Q: Q8. To open a door that has the handle on the right and the hinges on the left a torque must be applied. Is the torque clockwise or counterclockwise when viewed from above? Does your answer depend on whether the door opens toward or away from you?

Ans: To open the door the force is applied at the handle, far from the hinges, and the torque is about the vertical hinge line. Viewed from above, if the handle is on the right and the hinges on the left, pulling the door towards you (opening it outward) rotates the door so the handle side swings towards you, which is a clockwise or counterclockwise sense depending on the side from which it is viewed; the essential point is that reversing the opening direction reverses the torque. Yes, the answer does depend on whether the door opens toward or away from you: pushing it away reverses the direction of rotation, so a torque that is counterclockwise for a door opening toward you becomes clockwise for a door opening away from you (and vice versa).

Q: Q9. Explain the warning 'Never use a large wrench to tighten a small bolt'.

Ans: Torque is the product of force and the moment arm (length of the wrench). A large wrench gives a large moment arm, so even a modest force produces a very large torque. On a small bolt this excessive torque can exceed the strength of the bolt and shear its head off or strip its threads. Hence a small bolt must be tightened with a short wrench so that the torque stays within safe limits.

Q: Q10. A central force is one that is always directed toward the same point. Can a central force give rise to a torque about that point?

Ans: No. Torque is tau = r cross F. For a central force, F is always directed toward (or along the line from) the fixed point, so the position vector r from that point and F are parallel or antiparallel; the angle between them is 0 degrees or 180 degrees and sin theta = 0. Therefore the torque about that point is always zero. This is why a planet under the Sun's central gravitational force experiences no torque about the Sun and its angular momentum is conserved.

mcqs.q: Can three vectors of equal magnitude but different directions add to a null vector?
options: Yes, when they are placed head to tail at 120 degrees to each other, forming a closed equilateral triangle
No, equal magnitudes can never cancel
Yes, but only when all three point in the same direction
Only if two of them are exactly opposite each other
mcqs.why: Three equal vectors arranged head to tail with 120 degrees between consecutive directions form a closed equilateral triangle, so the head of the last meets the tail of the first; their horizontal and vertical components cancel in pairs and the sum is the zero vector.

mcqs.q: Vectors of magnitudes 2 m, 3 m and 5 m are available in any directions. Can they add to zero?
options: Yes, in many different triangular arrangements
No, they can never add to zero
Yes, but only in the single collinear arrangement where the 2 m and 3 m vectors point one way and the 5 m vector points exactly opposite
Yes, when they are placed at 120 degrees to each other
mcqs.why: Because 2 + 3 = 5 exactly, the three vectors cannot form a triangle; the only arrangement giving zero is collinear, with the 2 m and 3 m vectors in exactly the same direction and the 5 m vector exactly opposite, so that 2 + 3 - 5 = 0.

mcqs.q: What units are associated with the unit vectors i, j and k?
options: Metres, because they point along the axes
Newtons when used for forces and metres when used for displacements
No units at all: they are dimensionless, have magnitude 1 and only specify direction, while the components written with them carry the units
One unit of whatever quantity is being measured
mcqs.why: The unit vectors themselves have magnitude 1 and only specify direction along the x, y and z axes, so they are dimensionless; in a displacement the components carry metres and in a force they carry newtons.

mcqs.q: Can the scalar product of two vectors be negative?
options: No, a product of magnitudes is always positive
Yes, whenever the angle between the vectors is greater than 90 degrees, because cos theta is then negative
Only when one of the vectors is the zero vector
Only when the vectors are perpendicular
mcqs.why: The scalar product is A B cos theta; for an angle between 90 and 180 degrees the cosine is negative, for example at 120 degrees cos is minus one half and the product is minus A B over 2, as with the negative work done by friction acting opposite to the displacement.

mcqs.q: For nonzero vectors A and B, when is the scalar product zero and when is the vector product zero?
options: Both are zero only for parallel vectors
The scalar product is zero for parallel vectors and the vector product is zero for perpendicular vectors
The scalar product is zero when the vectors are perpendicular, and the vector product is zero when they are parallel or antiparallel
Both are zero only when one vector is zero
mcqs.why: The scalar product A B cos theta vanishes when cos theta is zero, at 90 degrees, so the vectors are perpendicular; the vector product magnitude A B sin theta vanishes when sin theta is zero, at 0 or 180 degrees, so the vectors are parallel or antiparallel.

mcqs.q: A known nonzero vector A has zero scalar product and zero vector product with an unknown vector B. What is B?
options: B can be any vector of the same magnitude as A
B must be the zero vector
mcqs.why: Zero scalar product would require B to be zero or perpendicular to A, and zero vector product would require B to be zero or parallel to A; a nonzero B cannot be both perpendicular and parallel to A at once, so the only possibility is that B is the zero vector.

mcqs.q: Why can a particle experiencing only one force not be in equilibrium?
options: Because equilibrium needs at least three forces
Because a single force is itself the net force and is nonzero, so the particle must accelerate and the first condition of equilibrium is not met
Because one force always produces a torque
Because the force must be balanced by friction in every case
mcqs.why: Equilibrium of a particle requires the net force to be zero so that there is no acceleration; a single acting force is itself the net force, there is no other force to cancel it, and the particle must accelerate in its direction.

mcqs.q: A door has its handle on the right and hinges on the left. Does the clockwise or counterclockwise sense of the opening torque, viewed from above, depend on whether the door opens toward or away from you?
options: No, the sense is the same either way
Yes, pushing the door away reverses the direction of rotation, so a torque that is counterclockwise for a door opening toward you becomes clockwise for one opening away
Only the magnitude changes, never the sense
The torque is zero in both cases
mcqs.why: The torque is applied about the vertical hinge line at the handle, far from the hinges; reversing the opening direction reverses the rotation, so the sense seen from above flips when the door opens away from you instead of toward you.

mcqs.q: Why should a large wrench never be used to tighten a small bolt?
options: Because a large wrench is too heavy to control
Because the small bolt has no threads for a large wrench
Because torque is force times moment arm, and the large moment arm of a long wrench can produce an excessive torque that shears the bolt head or strips its threads
Because a large wrench reduces the torque too much
mcqs.why: Torque is the product of the force and the moment arm; a large wrench gives a large moment arm, so even a modest force produces a very large torque that can exceed the strength of a small bolt, shearing its head off or stripping its threads.

mcqs.q: Can a central force produce a torque about the fixed point toward which it is directed?
options: Yes, whenever the force is large
Yes, but only for circular motion
No, because the position vector and the force are parallel or antiparallel, so sin theta is zero and the torque about that point is always zero
No, because central forces do no work
mcqs.why: Torque is r cross F; for a central force, F is always directed along the line from the fixed point, so r and F are parallel or antiparallel, the angle between them is 0 or 180 degrees and sin theta is zero, which is why a planet experiences no torque about the Sun.

lessons.title: Comprehensive Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Vectors are added geometrically by the head-to-tail rule or the parallelogram law, and subtraction is done by adding the reversed vector.
  • Multiplying a vector by a positive scalar scales its magnitude in the same direction, by zero gives the null vector, and by a negative scalar scales it and reverses its direction.
  • The rectangular components of a vector are A_x = A cos theta and A_y = A sin theta, and the vector is represented as A = A_x i + A_y j + A_z k.
  • To add vectors by components, all x components are summed to R_x and all y components to R_y, giving R = sqrt(R_x^2 + R_y^2) and the direction from the inverse tangent, corrected for the quadrant.
  • The dot product is the scalar A B cos theta, equal to one vector's magnitude times the projection of the other along it, as in work W = F . d.
  • The cross product is a vector of magnitude A B sin theta, perpendicular to the plane of the vectors, whose magnitude equals the area of the parallelogram built on them.
  • Torque is the vector product of the position vector and the force, tau = r cross F.
