The scale printed on the graph is 1 SD = 5 m/s and 1 SD = 1 s. Point A is at (0 s, 25 m/s). The line rises steadily to B, runs horizontal to C, falls steeply to D at (10 s, 10 m/s), then falls gently to E at (16 s, 0 m/s). Reading the top horizontal part with the scale, as in the book's printed answers, B is at (3 s, 50 m/s) and C is at (7 s, 50 m/s).
Given: A (0 s, 25 m/s), B (3 s, 50 m/s), C (7 s, 50 m/s), D (10 s, 10 m/s), E (16 s, 0 m/s)
Formula: a = (v_f - v_i) / (t_f - t_i), the slope of the velocity-time graph
Substitution (A to B): a = (50 - 25) / (3 - 0) = 25 / 3
Answer (A to B): 8.33 m/s^2
Substitution (B to C): a = (50 - 50) / (7 - 3) = 0 / 4
Answer (B to C): 0 m/s^2
Substitution (C to D): a = (10 - 50) / (10 - 7) = -40 / 3
Answer (C to D): -13.33 m/s^2
Substitution (D to E): a = (0 - 10) / (16 - 10) = -10 / 6
Answer (D to E): -1.67 m/s^2
Formula (average): a_avg = (v_E - v_A) / (t_E - t_A)
Substitution: a_avg = (0 - 25) / (16 - 0) = -25 / 16
Answer: Average acceleration for the complete journey = -1.56 m/s^2

Assignment 3.2 - Proton Passing Through Paper

Q: Q1. A proton moving with a speed of 1.0 x 10^7 m s^-1 passes through a 0.020 cm thick sheet of paper and emerges with a speed of 2.0 x 10^6 m s^-1. Assuming uniform deceleration, find retardation and time taken to pass through the paper.

Ans: Given: initial speed v_i = 1.0 x 10^7 m/s, final speed v_f = 2.0 x 10^6 m/s, thickness S = 0.020 cm = 2.0 x 10^-4 m
Formula: v_f^2 = v_i^2 + 2 a S, so a = (v_f^2 - v_i^2) / (2 S)
Substitution: a = ((2.0 x 10^6)^2 - (1.0 x 10^7)^2) / (2 x 2.0 x 10^-4)
a = (4.0 x 10^12 - 1.0 x 10^14) / (4.0 x 10^-4)
a = (-9.6 x 10^13) / (4.0 x 10^-4) = -2.4 x 10^17 m/s^2
The negative sign shows deceleration (retardation).
Formula: v_f = v_i + a t, so t = (v_f - v_i) / a
Substitution: t = (2.0 x 10^6 - 1.0 x 10^7) / (-2.4 x 10^17) = (-8.0 x 10^6) / (-2.4 x 10^17)
Answer: Retardation = -2.4 x 10^17 m/s^2 (magnitude 2.4 x 10^17 m/s^2), time taken = 3.3 x 10^-11 s

Assignment 3.3 - Astronaut and Spaceship

Q: Q1. Suppose that the mass of the spacecraft 'm_s' is 11 000 kg and that the mass of the astronaut 'm_A' is 92 kg. In addition, assume that the astronaut pushes with a force of F = + 36 N (along x-axis) on the spacecraft. Find the accelerations of the spacecraft and the astronaut.

Ans: Given: mass of spacecraft m_s = 11000 kg, mass of astronaut m_A = 92 kg, force on spacecraft F = +36 N along the x-axis
By Newton's third law, the spacecraft pushes back on the astronaut with a force of -36 N.
Formula: a = F / m
Substitution (spacecraft): a_s = (+36 N) / (11000 kg) = +0.00327 m/s^2
Substitution (astronaut): a_A = (-36 N) / (92 kg) = -0.39 m/s^2
Answer: a_s = +0.0033 m/s^2, a_A = -0.39 m/s^2. The astronaut, having the much smaller mass, gets the much larger acceleration, in the opposite direction.

Assignment 3.4 - Fire Emergency

Q: Q1. A girl of mass 48.0 kg is rescued from a building fire by leaping into a firefighters' net. The window from which she leapt was 12.0 m above the net. She lands in the net so that she is brought to a complete stop in 0.45 s. During this interval (a) What is his change in momentum? (b) What is the impulse on the net due to the girl? (c) What is the average force on the net due to the girl?

Ans: Given: mass m = 48.0 kg, height of fall h = 12.0 m, stopping time Delta t = 0.45 s, g = 9.8 m/s^2. Take downward as positive.
Formula: speed on reaching the net, v = sqrt(2 g h)
Substitution: v = sqrt(2 x 9.8 x 12.0) = sqrt(235.2) = 15.34 m/s
(a) Formula: change in momentum Delta p = m v_f - m v_i = 0 - m v
Substitution: Delta p = -(48.0 x 15.34) = -736 kg m/s
Answer (a): Change in momentum = 7.36 x 10^2 kg m/s (UP)
(b) During the stop, gravity also gives the girl an impulse of m g Delta t = 48.0 x 9.8 x 0.45 = 212 kg m/s (DOWN), so the impulse given to the girl by the net is 736 + 212 = 948 kg m/s (UP). By Newton's third law the impulse on the net due to the girl is equal and opposite.
Answer (b): Impulse on the net = 9.48 x 10^2 kg m/s (DOWN)
(c) Formula: F_avg = impulse / Delta t
Substitution: F_avg = 948 / 0.45 = 2107 N
Answer (c): Average force on the net = 2.11 x 10^3 N (DOWN)
Note: The book's printed answer ((a) 11.2 x 10^3 kg m s^-1 (UP), (b) 11.5 x 10^3 kg m s^-1 (DOWN), (c) 25.6 x 10^3 kg m s^-1 (DOWN)) is incorrect because a 48.0 kg girl falling 12.0 m reaches only 15.34 m/s, so her momentum is only 7.36 x 10^2 kg m/s, and part (c) is a force, whose unit is the newton, not kg m s^-1.

Assignment 3.5 - Elastic Collision Between Cars

Q: Q1. On a highway a car of mass 1500 kg is stopped at traffic signal. A pickup of mass 2000 kg comes up from behind and hits the stopped car. Assuming the collision is elastic, the pickup stops with collision and push the car ahead onto the highway at 10.0 m/s. How fast was the pickup going just before the collision?

Ans: Given: mass of pickup m_1 = 2000 kg, mass of car m_2 = 1500 kg, car initially at rest u_2 = 0, velocity of car after collision v_2 = 10.0 m/s, velocity of pickup before collision u_1 = ?
Formula: for an elastic collision with the second body at rest, v_2 = (2 m_1 / (m_1 + m_2)) x u_1
Substitution: 10.0 = (2 x 2000 / (2000 + 1500)) x u_1 = (4000 / 3500) x u_1
Working: u_1 = 10.0 x 3500 / 4000 = 8.75 m/s
Converting: 8.75 m/s x 3.6 = 31.5 km/h
Answer: The pickup was going at 8.75 m/s (31.5 km/hr) just before the collision.

Assignment 3.6 - Cricket Ball for a Six

Q: Q1. At Arbab Niaz Cricket Stadium Peshawar a batsman hits the shot at initial velocity of 28 m/s. If the boundary is 72 m from the batsman, will the ball cross the boundary for a six? If the angle with the horizontal is (a) 30 degrees (b) 45 degrees and (c) 70 degrees. (Ignore air resistance)

Ans: Given: initial velocity v_o = 28 m/s, boundary distance = 72 m, g = 9.8 m/s^2
Formula: Range R = (v_o^2 sin 2 theta) / g = (784 x sin 2 theta) / 9.8 = 80 x sin 2 theta
Substitution (a) theta = 30 degrees: R = 80 x sin 60 degrees = 80 x 0.866 = 69.2 m
Answer (a): No, R = 69.2 m, less than 72 m, so the ball does not cross the boundary.
Substitution (b) theta = 45 degrees: R = 80 x sin 90 degrees = 80 x 1 = 80 m
Answer (b): Yes, R = 80 m, more than 72 m, so the ball crosses the boundary for a six.
Substitution (c) theta = 70 degrees: R = 80 x sin 140 degrees = 80 x 0.643 = 51.4 m
Answer (c): No, R = 51.4 m, less than 72 m, so the ball does not cross the boundary.

Exercise - Numerical Questions

Q: Q1. An object is falling freely under gravity. How much distance will it travel in 2nd and 3rd second of its journey?

Ans: Given: object falling freely from rest, u = 0, g = 10 m/s^2 (the value used for the book's printed answers)
Formula: distance travelled in the nth second, S_n = u + (g / 2) (2n - 1) = (g / 2) (2n - 1)
Substitution (2nd second, n = 2): S_2 = (10 / 2) x (4 - 1) = 5 x 3 = 15 m
Substitution (3rd second, n = 3): S_3 = (10 / 2) x (6 - 1) = 5 x 5 = 25 m
Answer: 15 m in the 2nd second and 25 m in the 3rd second (15 m, 25 m)

Q: Q2. A helicopter is ascending vertically at a speed of 19.6 m s^-1. When it is at a height of 156.8 m above the ground, a stone is dropped. How long does the stone take to reach the ground?

Ans: Given: initial velocity of stone = velocity of helicopter = +19.6 m/s (upward), displacement to the ground S = -156.8 m, a = -g = -9.8 m/s^2. Take upward as positive.
Formula: S = v_i t + (1/2) a t^2
Substitution: -156.8 = 19.6 t - 4.9 t^2
Working: 4.9 t^2 - 19.6 t - 156.8 = 0, dividing by 4.9: t^2 - 4 t - 32 = 0
Working: (t - 8) (t + 4) = 0, so t = 8 s or t = -4 s
The negative time is impossible, so the positive value is taken. The stone first rises with the helicopter's upward velocity, stops, and then falls to the ground.
Answer: 8.0 s

Q: Q3. A car moving at 20.0 m/s (72.0 km/h) crashes into a tree. Find the magnitude of the average force acting on a passenger of mass 70 kg in each of the following cases. (a) The passenger is not wearing a seat belt. He is brought to rest by a collision with the windshield and dashboard that lasts 2.0 ms. (b) The car is equipped with a passenger-side air bag. The force due to the air bag acts for 45 ms, bringing the passenger to rest.

Ans: Given: mass m = 70 kg, initial velocity v_i = 20.0 m/s, final velocity v_f = 0
Formula: change in momentum Delta p = m (v_f - v_i), and F_avg = Delta p / Delta t
Substitution: Delta p = 70 x (0 - 20.0) = -1400 kg m/s, magnitude 1400 kg m/s
(a) Substitution: Delta t = 2.0 ms = 2.0 x 10^-3 s, F = 1400 / (2.0 x 10^-3) = 700000 N
Answer (a): 7.0 x 10^5 N
(b) Substitution: Delta t = 45 ms = 45 x 10^-3 s, F = 1400 / (45 x 10^-3) = 31111 N
Answer (b): 3.1 x 10^4 N. The air bag increases the stopping time, so the average force is reduced more than twenty times.

Q: Q4. A 0.4 kg ball traveling with the speed of 15 m s^-1 strikes a rigid wall and rebounds elastically. If the ball is in contact with the wall for 0.045 s, what is (a) the momentum imparted to the wall and (b) the average force exerted on the wall?

Ans: Given: mass m = 0.4 kg, initial velocity v_i = +15 m/s, final velocity after elastic rebound v_f = -15 m/s, contact time Delta t = 0.045 s
Formula: change in momentum of the ball, Delta p = m v_f - m v_i
Substitution: Delta p = 0.4 x (-15) - 0.4 x (15) = -6 - 6 = -12 kg m/s
(a) The momentum imparted to the wall is equal and opposite to the change of the ball.
Answer (a): 12 kg m s^-1 imparted to the wall
(b) Formula: F_avg = (momentum imparted) / Delta t
Substitution: F_avg = 12 / 0.045 = 266.7 N
Answer (b): Average force exerted on the wall = 266.7 N

Q: Q5. One ball of mass 0.600 kg traveling 9.00 m/s to the right collides head on elastically with a second ball of mass 0.300 kg traveling 8.00 m/s to the left. After the collision, what are their velocities after collision?

Ans: Given: m_1 = 0.600 kg, u_1 = +9.00 m/s (to the right, taken as positive), m_2 = 0.300 kg, u_2 = -8.00 m/s (to the left)
Formula: v_1 = ((m_1 - m_2) / (m_1 + m_2)) u_1 + ((2 m_2) / (m_1 + m_2)) u_2
Substitution: v_1 = ((0.600 - 0.300) / 0.900) x 9.00 + ((2 x 0.300) / 0.900) x (-8.00) = (0.333 x 9.00) + (0.667 x -8.00) = 3.00 - 5.33 = -2.33 m/s
Formula: v_2 = ((2 m_1) / (m_1 + m_2)) u_1 + ((m_2 - m_1) / (m_1 + m_2)) u_2
Substitution: v_2 = ((2 x 0.600) / 0.900) x 9.00 + ((0.300 - 0.600) / 0.900) x (-8.00) = (1.333 x 9.00) + (-0.333 x -8.00) = 12.00 + 2.67 = 14.67 m/s
Check (momentum): before = 0.600 x 9.00 + 0.300 x (-8.00) = 3.00 kg m/s; after = 0.600 x (-2.33) + 0.300 x 14.67 = 3.00 kg m/s. Conserved, as required.
Answer: First ball: -2.33 m/s, i.e. 2.33 m/s to the left. Second ball: 14.67 m/s to the right.
Note: The book's printed answer (- 2.33 m/s (2.33 m/s to right) and 14.67 m/s (14.76 m/s to left)) is incorrect because the negative sign on -2.33 m/s already means the first ball rebounds to the left, not the right, the second ball moves to the right, not the left, and 14.76 is a misprint for 14.67.

Q: Q6. In a wedding a bullet is fired in air at a speed of 500 m/s making an angle of 60 degrees with horizontal from an AK 47 rifle. (a) How high will the bullet rise? (b) What time would it take to reach ground? (c) How far would it go? (Ignore air resistance)

Ans: Given: v_o = 500 m/s, theta = 60 degrees, g = 9.8 m/s^2
(a) Formula: H = (v_o^2 sin^2 theta) / (2 g)
Substitution: H = ((500)^2 x (sin 60 degrees)^2) / (2 x 9.8) = (250000 x 0.75) / 19.6 = 187500 / 19.6 = 9566 m
Answer (a): About 9,560 m
(b) Formula: T = (2 v_o sin theta) / g
Substitution: T = (2 x 500 x 0.866) / 9.8 = 866 / 9.8 = 88.4 s
Answer (b): About 88.3 s
(c) Formula: R = (v_o^2 sin 2 theta) / g
Substitution: R = (250000 x sin 120 degrees) / 9.8 = (250000 x 0.866) / 9.8 = 216500 / 9.8 = 22092 m
Answer (c): About 22,078 m (22092 m by direct calculation; the small difference is rounding)

Q: Q7. The catapult hurls a stone of mass 32.0 g with a velocity of 50.0 m/s at a 30.0 degrees angle of elevation. (a) What is the maximum height reached by the stone? (b) What is its range? (c) How long has the stone been in the air when it returns to its original height?

Ans: Given: mass = 32.0 g (not needed for the kinematics), v_o = 50.0 m/s, theta = 30.0 degrees, g = 9.8 m/s^2
(a) Formula: H = (v_o^2 sin^2 theta) / (2 g)
Substitution: H = ((50.0)^2 x (sin 30 degrees)^2) / (2 x 9.8) = (2500 x 0.25) / 19.6 = 625 / 19.6 = 31.89 m
Answer (a): 31.87 m
(b) Formula: R = (v_o^2 sin 2 theta) / g
Substitution: R = (2500 x sin 60 degrees) / 9.8 = (2500 x 0.866) / 9.8 = 2165 / 9.8 = 220.9 m
Answer (b): 220.8 m
(c) Formula: T = (2 v_o sin theta) / g
Substitution: T = (2 x 50.0 x 0.5) / 9.8 = 50.0 / 9.8 = 5.10 s
Answer (c): 5.1 s
Note: The book's printed answer ((a) 31.87 m (b) 5.1 s (c) 220.8 m) is incorrect because the values for parts (b) and (c) are interchanged: 5.1 s is the time of flight asked in (c), and 220.8 m is the range asked in (b).

mcqs.q: The velocity time graph shows the motion of car in a straight line. By reading the scale carefully, calculate (a) the acceleration of the car between segment A and B, B and C, C and D and D and E, from the slope of the graph. Also (b) Calculate the car's average acceleration for the complete journey. (Give the average acceleration for the complete journey.)
mcqs.why: Formula: average acceleration = (final velocity - initial velocity) / total time. Substitution: a_avg = (0 - 25) / (16 - 0) = -25 / 16. Step: -25 / 16 = -1.5625. Result: average acceleration for the complete journey = -1.56 m/s^2, using only the end points A and E of the graph.

mcqs.q: A proton moving with a speed of 1.0 x 10^7 m s^-1 passes through a 0.020 cm thick sheet of paper and emerges with a speed of 2.0 x 10^6 m s^-1. Assuming uniform deceleration, find retardation and time taken to pass through the paper. (Give the magnitude of the retardation.)
mcqs.why: Formula: v_f^2 = v_i^2 + 2 a S, so a = (v_f^2 - v_i^2) / (2 S). Substitution: a = ((2.0 x 10^6)^2 - (1.0 x 10^7)^2) / (2 x 2.0 x 10^-4) = (4.0 x 10^12 - 1.0 x 10^14) / (4.0 x 10^-4). Step: numerator = -9.6 x 10^13, and -9.6 x 10^13 / 4.0 x 10^-4 = -2.4 x 10^17. Result: retardation has magnitude 2.4 x 10^17 m/s^2, the negative sign showing deceleration.

mcqs.q: Suppose that the mass of the spacecraft 'm_s' is 11 000 kg and that the mass of the astronaut 'm_A' is 92 kg. In addition, assume that the astronaut pushes with a force of F = + 36 N (along x-axis) on the spacecraft. Find the accelerations of the spacecraft and the astronaut. (Give the acceleration of the astronaut.)
mcqs.why: Formula: a = F / m, with the reaction force on the astronaut equal and opposite to the push, F = -36 N by Newton's third law. Substitution: a_A = (-36 N) / (92 kg). Step: -36 / 92 = -0.391. Result: the astronaut's acceleration is -0.39 m/s^2, much larger than the spacecraft's because the astronaut's mass is much smaller.

mcqs.q: A girl of mass 48.0 kg is rescued from a building fire by leaping into a firefighters' net. The window from which she leapt was 12.0 m above the net. She lands in the net so that she is brought to a complete stop in 0.45 s. During this interval (a) What is his change in momentum? (b) What is the impulse on the net due to the girl? (c) What is the average force on the net due to the girl? (Give the average force on the net due to the girl, part (c).)
mcqs.why: Formula: speed at the net v = sqrt(2 g h), impulse on the net = m v + m g Delta t, and F_avg = impulse / Delta t. Substitution: v = sqrt(2 x 9.8 x 12.0) = 15.34 m/s, so the momentum change is 48.0 x 15.34 = 736 kg m/s and gravity adds 48.0 x 9.8 x 0.45 = 212 kg m/s, giving an impulse of 948 kg m/s on the net. Step: F_avg = 948 / 0.45 = 2107 N. Result: average force on the net = 2.11 x 10^3 N downward. Note: the book's printed answer of 25.6 x 10^3 is wrong, and its unit is also wrong, because a 48.0 kg girl falling 12.0 m reaches only 15.34 m/s and a force must be in newtons.

mcqs.q: On a highway a car of mass 1500 kg is stopped at traffic signal. A pickup of mass 2000 kg comes up from behind and hits the stopped car. Assuming the collision is elastic, the pickup stops with collision and push the car ahead onto the highway at 10.0 m/s. How fast was the pickup going just before the collision?
mcqs.why: Formula: for an elastic collision with the second body at rest, v_2 = (2 m_1 / (m_1 + m_2)) x u_1. Substitution: 10.0 = (2 x 2000 / (2000 + 1500)) x u_1 = (4000 / 3500) x u_1. Step: u_1 = 10.0 x 3500 / 4000 = 8.75. Result: the pickup was travelling at 8.75 m/s (31.5 km/h) just before the collision.

mcqs.q: At Arbab Niaz Cricket Stadium Peshawar a batsman hits the shot at initial velocity of 28 m/s. If the boundary is 72 m from the batsman, will the ball cross the boundary for a six? If the angle with the horizontal is (a) 30 degrees (b) 45 degrees and (c) 70 degrees. (Ignore air resistance) (Give the range when the angle is 45 degrees.)
mcqs.why: Formula: range R = (v_o^2 sin 2 theta) / g. Substitution: R = (28^2 x sin 90 degrees) / 9.8 = (784 x 1) / 9.8. Step: 784 / 9.8 = 80. Result: R = 80 m at 45 degrees, which is more than the 72 m boundary, so this hit does cross the boundary for a six.

mcqs.q: An object is falling freely under gravity. How much distance will it travel in 2nd and 3rd second of its journey? (Give the distance travelled in the 3rd second.)
mcqs.why: Formula: distance in the nth second from rest, S_n = (g / 2)(2n - 1), using g = 10 m/s^2 as in the solved answer. Substitution: for n = 3, S_3 = (10 / 2) x (6 - 1) = 5 x 5. Step: 5 x 5 = 25. Result: the object travels 25 m in the 3rd second (and 15 m in the 2nd second).

mcqs.q: A helicopter is ascending vertically at a speed of 19.6 m s^-1. When it is at a height of 156.8 m above the ground, a stone is dropped. How long does the stone take to reach the ground?
mcqs.why: Formula: S = v_i t + (1/2) a t^2, taking upward as positive so S = -156.8 m, v_i = +19.6 m/s and a = -9.8 m/s^2. Substitution: -156.8 = 19.6 t - 4.9 t^2. Step: rearranging and dividing by 4.9 gives t^2 - 4 t - 32 = 0, which factorises as (t - 8)(t + 4) = 0. Result: t = 8.0 s, rejecting the impossible negative root; the stone first rises, stops, then falls.

mcqs.q: A car moving at 20.0 m/s (72.0 km/h) crashes into a tree. Find the magnitude of the average force acting on a passenger of mass 70 kg in each of the following cases. (a) The passenger is not wearing a seat belt. He is brought to rest by a collision with the windshield and dashboard that lasts 2.0 ms. (b) The car is equipped with a passenger-side air bag. The force due to the air bag acts for 45 ms, bringing the passenger to rest. (Give the average force in the air-bag case, part (b).)
mcqs.why: Formula: F_avg = change in momentum / stopping time, with change in momentum = m (v_f - v_i). Substitution: change in momentum = 70 x (0 - 20.0) = -1400 kg m/s, magnitude 1400, and the air bag acts for 45 ms = 45 x 10^-3 s. Step: F = 1400 / (45 x 10^-3) = 31111 N. Result: average force = 3.1 x 10^4 N, more than twenty times smaller than the 7.0 x 10^5 N without a seat belt, because the stopping time is longer.

mcqs.q: One ball of mass 0.600 kg traveling 9.00 m/s to the right collides head on elastically with a second ball of mass 0.300 kg traveling 8.00 m/s to the left. After the collision, what are their velocities after collision? (Give the velocity of the second ball after the collision.)
mcqs.why: Formula: v_2 = ((2 m_1) / (m_1 + m_2)) u_1 + ((m_2 - m_1) / (m_1 + m_2)) u_2. Substitution: v_2 = ((2 x 0.600) / 0.900) x 9.00 + ((0.300 - 0.600) / 0.900) x (-8.00) = (1.333 x 9.00) + (-0.333 x -8.00). Step: 12.00 + 2.67 = 14.67. Result: the second ball moves off at 14.67 m/s to the right. Note: the book's printed answer is wrong because it sends this ball to the left and misprints its speed as 14.76 m/s.

lessons.title: Multiple Choice Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • When a crate slides down a ramp at constant velocity, friction does the greatest magnitude of work because it must balance both gravity's component and the push.
  • For wires stretched through the same distance, the work done is proportional to the force constant, so a wire of constant 3k needs three times the work.
  • Escape velocity varies as the square root of (mass / radius), so doubling Earth's mass and halving its radius would raise it to 22.4 km/s.
  • Friction is a non-conservative force, while gravitational, electric and magnetic forces are conservative.
  • Kinetic energy varies with the square of the speed, so doubling a car's speed makes its kinetic energy four times greater.
  • One horsepower is equal to 746 W.
  • Work is negative when the force and displacement are anti-parallel, and for bodies of equal momentum the kinetic energies are in the inverse ratio of the masses.
  • If the momentum of a body increases by 20 percent, its kinetic energy increases by 44 percent.

Solved Exercises

Exercise - Multiple Choice Questions

Q: Q1. You push a heavy crate down a ramp at a constant velocity. Only four forces act on the crate. Which force does the greatest magnitude of work on the crate?

Options: (a) The force of friction. (b) The force of gravity. (c) The normal force. (d) The force you pushing.

Correct answer: The force of friction.

Q: Q2. The force constant of a wire is k and that of the another wire is 3k when both the wires are stretched through same distance, if work done are W_1 and W_2, then

Options: (a) W_2 = W_1 (b) W_2 = 9 W_1 (c) W_1 = 3 W_2 (d) W_2 = 3 W_1

Correct answer: W_2 = 3 W_1

Q: Q3. Escape velocity on the surface of the earth is 11.2 kms^-1. If the mass of the earth increases to twice its value and the radius of the earth becomes half the escape velocity is

Options: (a) 5.6 kms^-1 (b) 11.2 kms^-1 (c) 22.4 kms^-1 (d) 33.6 kms^-1

Correct answer: 22.4 kms^-1

Q: Q4. An example of non-conservative force is:

Options: (a) Electric force (b) Gravitational Force (c) Frictional force (d) Magnetic force

Correct answer: Frictional force

Q: Q5. When the speed of your car is doubled, by what factor does its kinetic energy increase?

Options: (a) sqrt(2). (b) 2. (c) 4. (d) 8.

Correct answer: 4.

Q: Q6. One horse power is given by:

Options: (a) 746 W (b) 746 KW (c) 746 MW (d) 746 GW

Correct answer: 746 W

Q: Q7. Work is said to be negative when F and d are:

Options: (a) Parallel (b) Anti Parallel (c) Perpendicular (d) at 45 degrees

Correct answer: Anti Parallel

Q: Q8. Two bodies of masses m_1 and m_2 have equal momentum their kinetic energies E_1 and E_2 are in the ratio

Options: (a) sqrt(m_1) : sqrt(m_2) (b) m_1 : m_2 (c) m_2 : m_1 (d) sqrt(m_1^2) : sqrt(m_2^2)

Correct answer: m_2 : m_1

Q: Q9. The atmosphere is held to the earth by

Options: (a) Winds (b) Gravity (c) Clouds (d) The rotation of earth

Correct answer: Gravity

Q: Q10. If momentum is increased by 20% then k.E increases by

Options: (a) 44% (b) 55% (c) 66% (d) 77%

Correct answer: 44%

Q: Q11. If the k.E of a body becomes four times of the initial value, then new momentum will

Options: (a) Become twice its initial value (b) Become three times, its initial value (c) Become four times, its initial value (d) Remains constant.

Correct answer: Become twice its initial value

Q: Q12. Two bodies with kinetic energies in the ratio of 4 : 1 are moving with equal linear momentum. The ratio of their masses is

Options: (a) 1 : 2 (b) 1 : 1 (c) 4 : 1 (d) 1 : 4

Correct answer: 1 : 4

Q: Q13. A body of mass 5 kg is moving with a momentum of 10 kg ms^-1. A force of 0.2 N acts on it in the direction of motion of the body for 10s. The increase in its kinetic energy is

Options: (a) 2.8 J (b) 3.2 J (c) 3.8 J (d) 4.4 J

Correct answer: 4.4 J

Q: Q14. If force and displacement of particle in the direction of force are doubled. Work would be

Options: (a) Double (b) 4 times (c) Half (d) 1/4 times

Correct answer: 4 times

mcqs.q: You push a heavy crate down a ramp at a constant velocity. Only four forces act on the crate. Which force does the greatest magnitude of work on the crate?
mcqs.why: At constant velocity the forces balance, so friction must oppose both the component of gravity along the ramp and the push; its work therefore has the greatest magnitude, while the normal force does no work at all.

mcqs.q: The force constant of a wire is k and that of the another wire is 3k when both the wires are stretched through same distance, if work done are W_1 and W_2, then
mcqs.why: Work stored in a stretched wire is one-half k x squared; for the same stretch x the work is proportional to k, so tripling k from k to 3k triples the work, giving W_2 = 3 W_1.

mcqs.q: Escape velocity on the surface of the earth is 11.2 kms^-1. If the mass of the earth increases to twice its value and the radius of the earth becomes half the escape velocity is
mcqs.why: Escape velocity is the square root of (2 G M / R); doubling M and halving R multiplies the quantity inside the root by four, so the escape velocity doubles from 11.2 to 22.4 km/s.

mcqs.q: An example of non-conservative force is:
mcqs.why: The work done by friction depends on the path taken and mechanical energy is lost as heat, which makes friction non-conservative, unlike gravity, the electric force and the magnetic force.

mcqs.q: When the speed of your car is doubled, by what factor does its kinetic energy increase?
mcqs.why: Kinetic energy is one-half m v squared, so it depends on the square of the speed; doubling the speed multiplies the kinetic energy by two squared, which is four.

mcqs.q: One horse power is given by:
mcqs.why: The horsepower is a daily-life unit of power defined as 746 watts, not kilowatts or any larger multiple of the watt.

mcqs.q: Work is said to be negative when F and d are:
mcqs.why: Work is F d cos of the angle between force and displacement; when the two are anti-parallel the angle is 180 degrees, cos is -1, and the work is negative, as with friction opposing motion.

mcqs.q: Two bodies of masses m_1 and m_2 have equal momentum their kinetic energies E_1 and E_2 are in the ratio
mcqs.why: Writing kinetic energy as p squared divided by (2 m) shows that for equal momenta the kinetic energies are inversely proportional to the masses, so E_1 : E_2 = m_2 : m_1.

mcqs.q: The atmosphere is held to the earth by
mcqs.why: The atmosphere's gases are pulled toward the Earth and kept from escaping into space by the Earth's gravitational attraction, not by winds, clouds or rotation.

mcqs.q: If momentum is increased by 20% then k.E increases by
mcqs.why: Kinetic energy is proportional to the square of the momentum, so a 20 percent rise in momentum multiplies kinetic energy by 1.2 squared = 1.44, an increase of 44 percent.

mcqs.q: If the k.E of a body becomes four times of the initial value, then new momentum will
options: Become three times, its initial value
Become four times, its initial value
mcqs.why: Since kinetic energy is p squared divided by (2 m), making the kinetic energy four times greater multiplies p squared by four, so the momentum itself becomes twice its initial value.

mcqs.q: Two bodies with kinetic energies in the ratio of 4 : 1 are moving with equal linear momentum. The ratio of their masses is
mcqs.why: With equal momenta, kinetic energy is inversely proportional to mass, so a kinetic energy ratio of 4 : 1 means a mass ratio of 1 : 4.

mcqs.q: A body of mass 5 kg is moving with a momentum of 10 kg ms^-1. A force of 0.2 N acts on it in the direction of motion of the body for 10s. The increase in its kinetic energy is
mcqs.why: The impulse 0.2 N x 10 s = 2 kg m/s raises the momentum from 10 to 12 kg m/s; the kinetic energy rises from 10 J to 14.4 J, an increase of 4.4 J.

mcqs.q: If force and displacement of particle in the direction of force are doubled. Work would be
mcqs.why: Work is force multiplied by displacement, so doubling the force and also doubling the displacement multiplies the work by two times two, making it four times the original.

mcqs.q: The net work done on a body is equal to which of the following?
options: The body's final kinetic energy alone
The change in the body's kinetic energy
The body's momentum multiplied by its velocity
The power multiplied by the distance moved
mcqs.why: The work-energy principle states that the net work done on a body equals the change in its kinetic energy, one-half m v_f squared minus one-half m v_i squared, whether the body speeds up, slows down or keeps constant speed.

lessons.title: Conceptual Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Potential energy is measured relative to a chosen reference level, so a bucket at the bottom of a well has P.E. = -m g h relative to the top.
  • The kinetic energy of an arrow comes from the elastic potential energy stored in the drawn bow, which came from the archer's work.
  • Kinetic energy is a scalar quantity because it depends on the square of the speed and has no direction.
  • A bullet penetrating a target loses its kinetic energy to work against the resistive force, producing heat, sound and deformation.
  • The tension in a pendulum's string does no work because it acts at right angles to the bob's displacement at every instant.
  • A meteor's mechanical energy is converted by air friction into heat and light, which is why it glows and burns in the atmosphere.
  • The spring of a watch stores elastic potential energy when wound and releases it gradually to drive the mechanism.
  • A man rowing upstream but staying at rest relative to the shore does no work on the boat, because the boat has no displacement in that frame.

Solved Exercises

Exercise - Conceptual Questions

Q: Q1. A bucket is taken to the bottom of a well, does the bucket possess any P.E? Explain.

Ans: Potential energy depends on the reference level chosen. If the ground at the top of the well is taken as the zero of P.E., the bucket at the bottom, at depth h, has P.E. = -m g h, that is, it has less potential energy than at the top by m g h. Relative to the bottom itself its P.E. is zero, and relative to any lower level it would be positive. So the bucket does possess potential energy, but its value is meaningful only relative to the chosen reference; work would have to be done (m g h) to raise it back to the top.

Q: Q2. When an arrow is shot from its bow, it has k.E. From where does it get the k.E?

Ans: The archer does work in drawing the bowstring back, and this work is stored as elastic potential energy in the bent bow and stretched string. On release, the bow springs back and this stored elastic potential energy is transferred to the arrow as kinetic energy. So the arrow's K.E. comes from the elastic P.E. of the drawn bow, which in turn came from the work done by the archer's muscles (chemical energy of the body).

Q: Q3. Does a hydrogen filled balloon possess any P.E? Explain.

Ans: Yes, in the sense of the balloon-and-air system. A hydrogen balloon held at the ground can do work as it rises, for example it can lift a small load. As the light balloon rises, the heavier surrounding air effectively comes down to take its place, and the potential energy of the system changes. The balloon therefore possesses potential energy relative to the ground because of its position in the gravitational field together with the buoyant force; released, it converts this into kinetic energy of upward motion.

Q: Q4. Is k.E a vector quantity?

Ans: No. Kinetic energy, K.E. = (1/2) m v^2, depends on the square of the speed, so it is the same whatever the direction of motion. It has magnitude only and no direction, so it is a scalar quantity. (Momentum, m v, is the related vector quantity.)

Q: Q5. What happens to k.E of a bullet when it penetrates into a target?

Ans: The bullet does work against the resistive (frictional) force of the target material. Its kinetic energy is gradually converted into work done in tearing and pushing aside the material, and into heat and sound, until the bullet stops. The distance of penetration depends on the initial K.E. and the average opposing force, by work = force x penetration distance. No kinetic energy remains once the bullet is embedded at rest; it has all been changed into other forms, mainly heat and deformation.

Q: Q6. Does the tension in the string of a swinging pendulum do any work? Explain.

Ans: No. The bob moves along a circular arc, and its displacement at every instant is along the tangent to the arc, while the tension acts along the string, that is, radially, at right angles to the displacement. Since work W = F d cos theta and theta = 90 degrees, cos 90 degrees = 0, so the work done by tension is zero. Tension only changes the direction of the bob's velocity, not its speed; the speed changes because of the tangential component of gravity.

Q: Q7. A meteor when enters into the earth's atmosphere burns. What happens to its energy?

Ans: The meteor enters with a large kinetic energy (and potential energy). Friction with the air does negative work on it, converting its kinetic energy into heat and light energy, which is why it glows and burns up; some energy also goes into sound and into heating and ionising the air. The total energy remains constant in accordance with the law of conservation of energy; the meteor's mechanical energy is transformed, not destroyed.

Q: Q8. What type of energy is stored in the spring of watch?

Ans: Elastic potential energy. When the watch is wound, work is done in coiling the spring tighter, and this work is stored as elastic (strain) potential energy in the spring. The spring then gradually uncoils, releasing this stored energy to drive the hands and mechanism of the watch.

Q: Q9. A man drops a cup from a certain height, which breaks into pieces. What energy changes are involved?

Ans: At the height, the cup has gravitational potential energy. As it falls, P.E. is converted into kinetic energy, which is maximum just before impact. On striking the ground, the kinetic energy is converted into the work done in breaking the cup into pieces, into kinetic energy of the flying pieces, and into heat and sound energy. The pieces finally come to rest with less P.E. than the cup had at the top.

Q: Q10. A man rowing boat upstream is at rest with respect to shore, is he doing work?

Ans: With respect to the shore, the boat has no displacement, so no work is done on the boat in the physics sense, even though the man is working hard and using up chemical energy of his body. The work he does is done on the water: his oars push water downstream, giving the water kinetic energy, and this effort exactly balances the push of the current so that the boat stays in place. If the same rowing were judged in the frame of the water, the boat would be moving and work would be counted; work depends on the displacement in the chosen frame.

Q: Q11. Why energy savers are used instead of normal bulbs?

Ans: An energy saver (compact fluorescent or LED bulb) produces the same amount of light while consuming far less electrical energy than a normal incandescent bulb, in which most of the energy is wasted as heat and only a small part becomes light. Using energy savers therefore reduces electricity consumption and bills, reduces the load on power stations and fuel use, and the bulbs also last much longer.

mcqs.q: A bucket is lowered to the bottom of a well. Taking the ground at the top as the zero of potential energy, what is the bucket's potential energy at the bottom?
options: Positive, equal to m g h
It has no potential energy at any level
mcqs.why: Potential energy is meaningful only relative to a chosen reference level; at a depth h below the reference the bucket's potential energy is -m g h, and work equal to m g h would be needed to raise it back to the top.

mcqs.q: From where does an arrow shot from a bow get its kinetic energy?
options: From the elastic potential energy stored in the drawn bow and string
From the gravity acting on the arrow
From the air it pushes aside
It is created at the moment of release
mcqs.why: The archer's work in drawing the bowstring is stored as elastic potential energy in the bent bow and stretched string, and on release this stored energy is transferred to the arrow as kinetic energy.

mcqs.q: Is kinetic energy a vector quantity?
options: Yes, it points along the velocity
No, it is a scalar because it depends on the square of the speed
It is a vector only for rotating bodies
It has direction but no magnitude
mcqs.why: Kinetic energy equals one-half m v squared; because the speed is squared, the value is the same whatever the direction of motion, so kinetic energy has magnitude only and is a scalar, unlike momentum which is a vector.

mcqs.q: What happens to the kinetic energy of a bullet as it penetrates a target?
options: It stays stored in the bullet unchanged
It is converted into work against the resistive force, and into heat, sound and deformation of the target
It changes into potential energy of the target
mcqs.why: The bullet does work against the frictional resistance of the material, so its kinetic energy is gradually spent tearing and pushing the material aside and producing heat and sound, until no kinetic energy remains when the bullet stops.

mcqs.q: Does the tension in the string of a swinging pendulum do any work on the bob?
options: Yes, it speeds the bob up on the way down
No, because tension acts along the string, at right angles to the bob's displacement, so cos 90 degrees makes the work zero
Yes, but only at the ends of the swing
No, because the string is inextensible and exerts no force
mcqs.why: The bob moves along the tangent to its arc while the tension acts radially along the string, so the angle between force and displacement is 90 degrees and W = F d cos 90 degrees = 0; tension changes only the direction of motion, not the speed.

mcqs.q: A meteor burns up as it enters the Earth's atmosphere. What happens to its energy?
options: Its energy is destroyed by the burning
Its kinetic energy is converted by friction into heat and light energy, so total energy is conserved
Its energy changes entirely into potential energy
Its energy passes into the Earth's rotation
mcqs.why: Friction with the air does negative work on the fast meteor, converting its kinetic energy into heat and light, which is why it glows and burns; the total energy remains constant, only its form changes, in line with conservation of energy.

mcqs.q: What type of energy is stored in the spring of a wound watch?
mcqs.why: Winding the watch does work in coiling the spring tighter, and that work is stored as elastic, or strain, potential energy in the spring, which is then released gradually to drive the hands and mechanism.

mcqs.q: A cup dropped from a height breaks into pieces on the ground. Which energy change happens at the impact?
options: Potential energy changes directly into sound only
The kinetic energy is converted into work of breaking, kinetic energy of the pieces, heat and sound
Kinetic energy changes back into potential energy
No energy change occurs once the cup lands
mcqs.why: During the fall the cup's potential energy becomes kinetic energy, greatest just before impact; on striking the ground that kinetic energy is spent in breaking the cup, flinging the pieces, and producing heat and sound.

mcqs.q: A man rows a boat upstream but the boat stays at rest relative to the shore. Is he doing work on the boat?
options: Yes, because he is applying a force
Yes, because he is using up energy
No, because relative to the shore the boat has no displacement, so no work is done on it
Only if the current is faster than his rowing
mcqs.why: Work requires displacement in the chosen frame; relative to the shore the boat does not move, so no work is done on the boat, and the man's effort instead does work on the water, pushing it downstream to balance the current.

mcqs.q: Why are energy savers used instead of normal incandescent bulbs?
options: They produce the same light while consuming far less electrical energy, wasting much less as heat
They are brighter because they use more power
They convert all their energy into heat
mcqs.why: A normal bulb wastes most of its electrical energy as heat and turns only a small part into light, while an energy saver gives the same light for far less energy, cutting bills and the load on power stations, and lasting much longer.

lessons.title: Comprehensive Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Work is the scalar (dot) product of force and displacement, W = F d cos theta, measured in joules.
  • Work is maximum and positive when force and displacement are in the same direction, and most negative when they are opposite.
  • Power is the rate of doing work and is also the dot product of force and velocity, P = F . v.
  • Units of power in daily life include the watt, kilowatt and megawatt, and the horsepower, with 1 hp = 746 W.
  • The work-energy principle states that the net work done on a body equals the change in its kinetic energy.
  • The magnitude of the absolute potential energy of a body at the Earth's surface is G m M_e / R_e, taking potential energy at infinity as zero.
  • Escape velocity from Earth is found by equating one-half m v squared with G M_e m / R_e, giving 11.2 km/s.
  • Non-conventional sources of energy include solar, tidal, wave, biomass, geothermal and wind energy, all naturally replenished.

Solved Exercises

Exercise - Comprehensive Questions

Q: Q1. Define work and show that it is the dot product of force and displacement. At what conditions work done will be maximum or minimum?

Ans: Work is done when a force acts on a body and the body is displaced in the direction of the force. Work done W = F d cos theta, where F is the force, d the displacement and theta the angle between them.
The dot product of the force vector F and the displacement vector d is F . d = F d cos theta, which is exactly the expression for work. Hence work is the scalar (dot) product of force and displacement, W = F . d, and work is therefore a scalar quantity measured in joules.
Maximum work: theta = 0 degrees, force and displacement in the same direction, cos 0 degrees = 1, so W is maximum and positive, W_max = F d.
Minimum work: theta = 180 degrees, force opposite to displacement, cos 180 degrees = -1, so W is minimum (most negative), W_min = -F d, as for friction opposing motion. When theta = 90 degrees, cos 90 degrees = 0 and no work is done at all, as when a body is carried horizontally at constant height against gravity.

Q: Q2. Define power and show that power is the dot product of force and velocity. What are the different units of power used in our daily life?

Ans: Power is the rate of doing work, P = W / t. Its SI unit is the watt, 1 W = 1 J/s.
Proof: For a constant force, W = F . d. Dividing by the time t, P = W / t = F . (d / t). But d / t is the velocity v of the body, so P = F . v. Hence power is the dot product of force and velocity; only the component of force along the velocity contributes.
Units used in daily life: the watt (W) for lamps and small appliances, the kilowatt (kW = 1000 W) for heaters, motors and air conditioners, the megawatt (MW) for power stations, the kilowatt-hour (kWh) as the commercial unit of energy billed as one unit of electricity, and the horsepower (1 hp = 746 W) for car, motorcycle and pump engines.

Q: Q3. Explain the work energy principle in the cases of the change in k.E of body.

Ans: The work-energy principle states that the net work done on a body is equal to the change in its kinetic energy: W_net = Delta K.E. = (1/2) m v_f^2 - (1/2) m v_i^2.
Case 1, speeding up: if the net force acts in the direction of motion, the work is positive and the kinetic energy increases by the amount of work done, as when an engine accelerates a car.
Case 2, slowing down: if the net force opposes the motion, as with brakes and friction, the work is negative and the kinetic energy decreases by that amount, changing into heat.
Case 3, constant speed: if forces balance, or the force is perpendicular to the motion as in uniform circular motion, the net work is zero and the kinetic energy stays constant even though work may be done by individual forces.
The principle also covers falling bodies: the work done by gravity, m g h, appears exactly as the gain in kinetic energy of a falling body.

Q: Q4. Prove that Absolute P.E = (G m M_e) / R_e

Ans: Absolute potential energy of a body at the Earth's surface is the work that must be done to take it from the Earth's surface to infinity against gravity (equivalently, the work gravity does in bringing it from infinity to the surface), taking P.E. at infinity as zero.
The gravitational force at distance r from the Earth's centre is F = G M_e m / r^2, which decreases with distance, so the work is found by integrating from r = R_e to r = infinity: W = integral of F dr from R_e to infinity = G M_e m x [ -1 / r ] from R_e to infinity = G M_e m (0 + 1 / R_e) = G M_e m / R_e.
Hence the magnitude of the absolute P.E. at the surface is Absolute P.E. = G m M_e / R_e. (With the sign convention that P.E. at infinity is zero, the absolute P.E. at the surface is written -G M_e m / R_e; the expression above is its magnitude, the energy that must be supplied to free the body from Earth.)
This result is used to find the escape velocity by equating (1/2) m v_esc^2 with G M_e m / R_e.

Q: Q5. Calculate the values of the escape velocity of a body and show that it is equal 11.2 km s^-1.

Ans: Escape velocity is the minimum speed with which a body must be projected from the Earth so that it escapes the Earth's gravity and never returns.
Given: G = 6.67 x 10^-11 N m^2/kg^2, mass of Earth M_e = 6 x 10^24 kg, radius of Earth R_e = 6.4 x 10^6 m
Formula: equating kinetic energy with absolute P.E., (1/2) m v_esc^2 = G M_e m / R_e, so v_esc = sqrt(2 G M_e / R_e) = sqrt(2 g R_e)
Substitution: v_esc = sqrt((2 x 6.67 x 10^-11 x 6 x 10^24) / (6.4 x 10^6)) = sqrt(8.0 x 10^14 / 6.4 x 10^6) = sqrt(1.25 x 10^8)
Working: v_esc = 1.12 x 10^4 m/s
Answer: v_esc = 11.2 km s^-1, as required. Any body projected from Earth at 11.2 km/s or faster will escape Earth's gravity (neglecting air resistance).

Q: Q6. Describe briefly various non-conventional sources of energy.

Ans: Non-conventional (renewable) sources of energy are naturally replenished and do not run out. (a) Solar energy: sunlight converted directly into electricity by solar cells, and used in solar water heaters and cookers. (b) Energy from the tides: the rise and fall of sea tides in bays is used to drive turbines. (c) Energy from waves: the up-and-down motion of sea waves drives generators on floats or shore devices. (d) Energy from biomass: plant matter, animal dung and agricultural waste are burned directly or converted into biogas for cooking, heating and electricity. (e) Geothermal energy: heat from hot rocks and steam inside the Earth is used to generate electricity and for heating. Wind energy, from moving air driving wind turbines, is another major non-conventional source. These sources are clean and renewable, unlike coal, oil and gas, though some need costly equipment and suitable locations.

mcqs.q: Work done by a force is best described as:
options: The vector product of force and displacement
The scalar (dot) product of force and displacement, W = F d cos theta
Force multiplied by the time for which it acts
mcqs.why: The dot product of the force and displacement vectors is F d cos theta, which is exactly the expression for work, so work is a scalar quantity measured in joules even though force and displacement are both vectors.

mcqs.q: Under what condition is the work done by a force maximum and positive?
options: When the force is perpendicular to the displacement
When the force is opposite to the displacement
When the force and displacement are in the same direction, angle zero
When the angle between them is 45 degrees
mcqs.why: Work is F d cos theta, and cos theta is greatest, equal to 1, when the angle is zero, that is when force and displacement point the same way, giving the maximum positive work W = F d.

mcqs.q: A coolie carries a load horizontally at a steady height. How much work does he do against gravity?
options: F d, the full weight times distance
Half the weight times the distance
Zero, because the displacement is perpendicular to the gravitational force
Negative work equal to the weight times distance
mcqs.why: Gravity acts vertically downward while the displacement is horizontal, so the angle between them is 90 degrees and cos 90 degrees is zero; the work done against gravity is therefore zero, a case stated in the solved answer on maximum and minimum work.

mcqs.q: Power can be written as the dot product of which two quantities?
mcqs.why: Dividing the work W = F . d by the time t gives P = F . (d / t), and d / t is the velocity, so power equals the dot product of force and velocity and only the force component along the velocity contributes.

mcqs.q: One horsepower is equal to:
mcqs.why: The horsepower, used for car, motorcycle and pump engines, is defined as 746 watts, as listed among the daily-life units of power in the solved comprehensive answer.

mcqs.q: According to the work-energy principle, positive net work done on a body results in:
options: A decrease in its kinetic energy
An increase in its kinetic energy equal to the work done
No change in its kinetic energy
mcqs.why: The work-energy principle states W_net = change in kinetic energy; when the net force acts along the motion the work is positive and the kinetic energy grows by exactly that amount, as when an engine accelerates a car.

mcqs.q: When brakes slow a moving car down, the work-energy principle tells us that:
options: The negative work of the braking and friction forces reduces the kinetic energy, changing it into heat
The kinetic energy increases because the forces are large
No work is done because the car is decelerating
The kinetic energy is stored in the brakes unchanged
mcqs.why: Forces opposing the motion do negative work, so the change in kinetic energy is negative and the car loses kinetic energy equal to that work, the energy appearing mainly as heat in the brakes and tyres.

mcqs.q: Taking potential energy at infinity as zero, the magnitude of the absolute potential energy of a mass m at the Earth's surface is:
mcqs.why: Integrating the gravitational force G M_e m / r squared from the surface out to infinity gives the work G M_e m / R_e, which is the magnitude of the absolute potential energy at the surface and the energy that must be supplied to free the body from Earth.

mcqs.q: The escape velocity from the Earth, found by equating kinetic energy with absolute potential energy, is:
mcqs.why: Setting one-half m v squared equal to G M_e m / R_e gives v = square root of (2 G M_e / R_e); substituting G = 6.67 x 10^-11, M_e = 6 x 10^24 kg and R_e = 6.4 x 10^6 m gives the square root of 1.25 x 10^8, which is 1.12 x 10^4 m/s or 11.2 km/s.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is a non-conventional (renewable) source of energy?
options: Geothermal energy from hot rocks inside the Earth
mcqs.why: Non-conventional sources are naturally replenished and do not run out; geothermal energy, the heat of hot rocks and steam inside the Earth, is one of them, alongside solar, tidal, wave, biomass and wind energy, unlike coal, oil and gas.

lessons.title: Numerical Problems and Assignments
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Power is work divided by time, and the work in speeding a body up from rest equals its gain in kinetic energy, one-half m v squared.
  • The escape speed from a distance r from a planet's centre is the square root of (2 G M / r), giving 1441 m/s for the Moon's distance from Earth.
  • On a frictionless 100 m, 30-degree hill a sled starting at 2 m/s would reach 31.37 m/s at the bottom; friction in the solved case does -8840 J of work.
  • The work done by a force at an angle is F d cos theta, giving 4330 J for a 100 N pull over 50 m at 30 degrees.
  • A roller-coaster car dropping a net 15 m of height with mass 1000 kg loses 1.47 x 10^5 J as thermal energy, an average friction force of about 370 N over 400 m.
  • A 400 W engine working for 3 s does 1200 J of work and can lift a 100 kg mass through 1.22 m.
  • A body falling from rest gains speed v = square root of (2 g h), reaching 14 m/s after a 10 m fall from a bridge.
  • The escape velocity on the Moon is 2.5 km/s, because its mass is 1/80 and its radius 1/4 of Earth's.

Solved Exercises

Assignment 4.1

Q: Q1. What is the power of an airplane of mass 3 000 kg if when on the runway it is capable of reaching a speed of 80 ms^-1 from rest in 4.0 s?

Ans: Given: mass m = 3000 kg, initial speed = 0, final speed v = 80 m/s, time t = 4.0 s
Formula: Work done = gain in kinetic energy = (1/2) m v^2, and Power P = W / t
Substitution: W = (1/2) x 3000 x (80)^2 = 1500 x 6400 = 9.6 x 10^6 J
Substitution: P = (9.6 x 10^6) / 4.0 = 2.4 x 10^6 W
Answer: Power = 2.4 MW
Note: The book's printed answer (4.8 MW) is incorrect because it omits the factor 1/2 in the kinetic energy (1/2) m v^2, which doubles the result.

Assignment 4.2 - Gravitation Pull of Earth

Q: Q1. How fast would the moon need to travel in order to escape the gravitational pull of Earth, if Earth has a mass of 5.98 x 10^24 kg and the distance from Earth to the moon is 3.84 x 10^8 m?

Ans: Given: mass of Earth M = 5.98 x 10^24 kg, distance from Earth to moon r = 3.84 x 10^8 m, G = 6.67 x 10^-11 N m^2/kg^2
Formula: escape speed from a distance r, v_esc = sqrt(2 G M / r)
Substitution: v_esc = sqrt((2 x 6.67 x 10^-11 x 5.98 x 10^24) / (3.84 x 10^8))
Working: numerator = 2 x 6.67 x 5.98 x 10^13 = 7.98 x 10^14
Working: v_esc = sqrt(7.98 x 10^14 / 3.84 x 10^8) = sqrt(2.08 x 10^6) = 1441 m/s
Answer: The moon would need to travel at 1441 ms^-1 to escape the gravitational pull of Earth.

Assignment 4.3 - Friction

Q: Q1. Consider a person on a sled sliding down a 100 m long hill on a 30 degrees incline. The mass is 20 kg, and the person has a velocity of 2 ms^-1 down the hill when they're at the top. (a) How fast is the person traveling at the bottom of the hill? (b) If, the velocity at the bottom of the hill is 10 m s^-1, because of friction, how much work is done by friction?

Ans: Given: length of hill L = 100 m, incline theta = 30 degrees, mass m = 20 kg, initial velocity v_i = 2 m/s, g = 9.8 m/s^2
Formula: vertical height of the hill, h = L sin theta
Substitution: h = 100 x sin 30 degrees = 100 x 0.5 = 50 m
(a) Formula (conservation of energy, no friction): (1/2) m v_f^2 = (1/2) m v_i^2 + m g h, so v_f = sqrt(v_i^2 + 2 g h)
Substitution: v_f = sqrt((2)^2 + 2 x 9.8 x 50) = sqrt(4 + 980) = sqrt(984) = 31.37 m/s
Answer (a): 31.3 m s^-1
(b) Given: actual velocity at the bottom v_f = 10 m/s
Formula: work done by friction = total energy at bottom - total energy at top = ((1/2) m v_f^2) - ((1/2) m v_i^2 + m g h)
Substitution: W_f = (0.5 x 20 x 100) - (0.5 x 20 x 4 + 20 x 9.8 x 50) = 1000 - (40 + 9800) = 1000 - 9840
Answer (b): Work done by friction = -8840 J. The negative sign shows friction removes energy from the person.

Exercise - Numerical Questions

Q: Q1. A 70 kg man runs up a long flight of stairs in 4 s. The vertical height of the stair is 4.5m. Calculate his power.

Ans: Given: mass m = 70 kg, vertical height h = 4.5 m, time t = 4 s, g = 9.8 m/s^2
Formula: Work done W = m g h, Power P = W / t
Substitution: W = 70 x 9.8 x 4.5 = 3087 J
Substitution: P = 3087 / 4 = 771.75 W
Answer: P = 7.7 x 10^2 Watts

Q: Q2. A body of mass 2.0 kg is dropped from a rest position 5m above the ground. What is its velocity at height of 3.0 m above the ground?

Ans: Given: mass m = 2.0 kg, dropped from rest at height 5 m, velocity required at height 3.0 m, so distance fallen = 5 - 3.0 = 2.0 m, g = 9.8 m/s^2
Formula: by conservation of energy, loss in P.E. = gain in K.E., m g (2.0) = (1/2) m v^2, so v = sqrt(2 g x 2.0)
Substitution: v = sqrt(2 x 9.8 x 2.0) = sqrt(39.2) = 6.26 m/s
Answer: v = 6.3 m s^-1

Q: Q3. A man pulls a trolley through a distance of 50m by applying a force of 100N which makes an angle of 30 degrees with horizontal. Calculate the work done by the man.

Ans: Given: force F = 100 N, distance d = 50 m, angle theta = 30 degrees
Formula: W = F d cos theta
Substitution: W = 100 x 50 x cos 30 degrees = 5000 x 0.866 = 4330 J
Answer: Work done = 4330 J

Q: Q4. The roller-coaster car starts its journey from a vertical height of 40m on the first hill and reaches a vertical height of only 25m on the second hill, where it slows to a momentary stop. It traveled a total distance of 400 m. Determine the thermal energy produced and estimate the average friction force on the car whose mass is 1000 kg.

Ans: Given: mass m = 1000 kg, first height h_1 = 40 m, second height h_2 = 25 m, car momentarily at rest on both hills, total distance travelled d = 400 m, g = 9.8 m/s^2
Formula: thermal energy produced = loss in gravitational P.E. = m g (h_1 - h_2)
Substitution: Thermal energy = 1000 x 9.8 x (40 - 25) = 1000 x 9.8 x 15 = 147000 J
Answer: Thermal energy produced = 1.47 x 10^5 J
Formula: work done against friction = f x d = thermal energy, so f = thermal energy / d
Substitution: f = 147000 / 400 = 367.5 N
Answer: Average friction force = about 370 N

Q: Q5. A man whose mass is 70kg walks up to the third floor of a building which is 12m above the ground in 20s. Find his power in watts and hp.

Ans: Given: mass m = 70 kg, height h = 12 m, time t = 20 s, g = 9.8 m/s^2, 1 hp = 746 W
Formula: W = m g h, P = W / t
Substitution: W = 70 x 9.8 x 12 = 8232 J
Substitution: P = 8232 / 20 = 411.6 W
Substitution: P in hp = 411.6 / 746 = 0.55 hp
Answer: P = 411.6 watt = 0.55 hp

Q: Q6. To what height can a 400W engine lift a 100 kg mass in 3s?

Ans: Given: power P = 400 W, mass m = 100 kg, time t = 3 s, g = 9.8 m/s^2
Formula: Work done W = P t = m g h, so h = P t / (m g)
Substitution: W = 400 x 3 = 1200 J
Substitution: h = 1200 / (100 x 9.8) = 1200 / 980 = 1.22 m
Answer: h = 1.22 m
Note: The book's printed answer (h = 0.122 m) is incorrect because it is ten times too small: 400 W working for 3 s does 1200 J of work, and 1200 / (100 x 9.8) = 1.22 m, not 0.122 m.

Q: Q7. A ball of mass 100 g is thrown vertically upward at a speed of 25 ms^-1. If no energy is lost, determine the height it would reach. If the ball only rises to 25m, calculate the work done against air resistance. Also calculate the force of friction.

Ans: Given: mass m = 100 g = 0.1 kg, initial speed v = 25 m/s, actual height reached = 25 m, g = 9.8 m/s^2
Formula (no energy loss): loss in K.E. = gain in P.E., (1/2) m v^2 = m g h, so h = v^2 / (2 g)
Substitution: h = (25 x 25) / (2 x 9.8) = 625 / 19.6 = 31.9 m
Answer: Height with no energy loss = 31.9 m
Formula: work done against air resistance = initial K.E. - P.E. at 25 m = (1/2) m v^2 - m g h
Substitution: Initial K.E. = 0.5 x 0.1 x 625 = 31.25 J; P.E. at 25 m = 0.1 x 9.8 x 25 = 24.5 J
Working: Work against air resistance = 31.25 - 24.5 = 6.75 J, about 6.7 J
Formula: force of friction f = (work against resistance) / h
Substitution: f = 6.75 / 25 = 0.27 N
Answer: 31.9 m, 6.7 J, 0.3 N (0.27 N before rounding)

Q: Q8. An object of mass 1000 g falls from a height of 30m on the sand below. If it penetrates 4cm into the sand, what opposing force is exerted on it by the sand? Neglect air friction.

Ans: Given: mass m = 1000 g = 1 kg, height of fall h = 30 m, penetration into sand d = 4 cm = 0.04 m, g = 9.8 m/s^2
Formula: the gravitational energy lost in falling h + d is spent in doing work against the sand's opposing force f over distance d: m g (h + d) = f d, so f = m g (h + d) / d
Substitution: f = (1 x 9.8 x (30 + 0.04)) / 0.04 = (9.8 x 30.04) / 0.04 = 294.4 / 0.04 = 7360 N
Answer: f = about 7350 N (7360 N when the extra 4 cm fall during penetration is included)
Note: The book's printed answer (f = 7350 N) is obtained by neglecting the extra 4 cm fall during penetration, i.e. using f = m g h / d = 294 / 0.04 = 7350 N.

Q: Q9. A body of mass 'm' drops from Bridge into water of the river. The bridge is 10m high from the water surface. (a). Find the speed of the body 5m above the water surface. (b). Find the speed of the body before it strikes the water.

Ans: Given: bridge height = 10 m, body dropped from rest, g = 9.8 m/s^2
(a) The body is 5 m above the water, so it has fallen 10 - 5 = 5 m.
Formula: v = sqrt(2 g x distance fallen)
Substitution: v = sqrt(2 x 9.8 x 5) = sqrt(98) = 9.9 m/s
Answer (a): 9.9 m s^-1
(b) The body falls the full 10 m before striking the water.
Formula: v = sqrt(2 g h)
Substitution: v = sqrt(2 x 9.8 x 10) = sqrt(196) = 14 m/s
Answer (b): 14 m s^-1

Q: Q10. The engine of a JF-Thunder fighter (made by Pakistan and China) develops a thrust of 3000N. What horsepower does it at a velocity of 600 m s^-1?

Ans: Given: thrust (force) F = 3000 N, velocity v = 600 m/s, 1 hp = 746 W
Formula: Power P = F v
Substitution: P = 3000 x 600 = 1.8 x 10^6 W
Substitution: P in hp = (1.8 x 10^6) / 746 = 2413 hp
Answer: 2413 hp

Q: Q11. The mass of the moon is 1/80 of the mass of the earth and corresponding radius is 1/4 of the earth. Calculate the escape velocity on the surface of moon.

Ans: Given: mass of moon M_m = M_e / 80, radius of moon R_m = R_e / 4, escape velocity on Earth v_e = 11.2 km/s
Formula: v_esc = sqrt(2 G M / R), so v_moon / v_earth = sqrt((M_m / M_e) x (R_e / R_m))
Substitution: v_moon = 11.2 x sqrt((1/80) x (4/1)) = 11.2 x sqrt(4/80) = 11.2 x sqrt(0.05)
Working: sqrt(0.05) = 0.2236, so v_moon = 11.2 x 0.2236 = 2.50 km/s
Answer: Escape velocity on the surface of the moon = 2.5 kms^-1

mcqs.q: What is the power of an airplane of mass 3 000 kg if when on the runway it is capable of reaching a speed of 80 ms^-1 from rest in 4.0 s?
mcqs.why: Formula: work done = gain in kinetic energy = (1/2) m v^2, and power P = W / t. Substitution: W = (1/2) x 3000 x (80)^2 = 1500 x 6400 = 9.6 x 10^6 J, and P = (9.6 x 10^6) / 4.0. Step: 9.6 x 10^6 / 4.0 = 2.4 x 10^6 W. Result: power = 2.4 MW. Note: the book's printed answer of 4.8 MW is wrong because it omits the factor one-half in the kinetic energy, which doubles the result.

mcqs.q: How fast would the moon need to travel in order to escape the gravitational pull of Earth, if Earth has a mass of 5.98 x 10^24 kg and the distance from Earth to the moon is 3.84 x 10^8 m?
mcqs.why: Formula: escape speed from distance r, v_esc = sqrt(2 G M / r). Substitution: v_esc = sqrt((2 x 6.67 x 10^-11 x 5.98 x 10^24) / (3.84 x 10^8)). Step: the numerator is 7.98 x 10^14, dividing by 3.84 x 10^8 gives 2.08 x 10^6, and the square root of that is 1441. Result: the Moon would need to travel at 1441 m/s to escape Earth's pull from its orbit distance.

mcqs.q: Consider a person on a sled sliding down a 100 m long hill on a 30 degrees incline. The mass is 20 kg, and the person has a velocity of 2 ms^-1 down the hill when they're at the top. (a) How fast is the person traveling at the bottom of the hill? (b) If, the velocity at the bottom of the hill is 10 m s^-1, because of friction, how much work is done by friction? (Give the work done by friction in part (b).)
mcqs.why: Formula: height h = L sin theta, and work done by friction = total energy at the bottom minus total energy at the top. Substitution: h = 100 x sin 30 degrees = 50 m, so W_f = (0.5 x 20 x 10^2) - (0.5 x 20 x 2^2 + 20 x 9.8 x 50) = 1000 - (40 + 9800). Step: 1000 - 9840 = -8840. Result: work done by friction = -8840 J, the negative sign showing that friction removes energy from the person.

mcqs.q: A man pulls a trolley through a distance of 50m by applying a force of 100N which makes an angle of 30 degrees with horizontal. Calculate the work done by the man.
mcqs.why: Formula: W = F d cos theta. Substitution: W = 100 x 50 x cos 30 degrees = 5000 x 0.866. Step: 5000 x 0.866 = 4330. Result: work done by the man = 4330 J, less than F d because only the component of the force along the displacement does work.

mcqs.q: The roller-coaster car starts its journey from a vertical height of 40m on the first hill and reaches a vertical height of only 25m on the second hill, where it slows to a momentary stop. It traveled a total distance of 400 m. Determine the thermal energy produced and estimate the average friction force on the car whose mass is 1000 kg. (Give the average friction force on the car.)
mcqs.why: Formula: thermal energy = loss in gravitational P.E. = m g (h_1 - h_2), and average friction force f = thermal energy / total distance. Substitution: thermal energy = 1000 x 9.8 x (40 - 25) = 147000 J, and f = 147000 / 400. Step: 147000 / 400 = 367.5. Result: average friction force is about 370 N, and the thermal energy produced is 1.47 x 10^5 J.

mcqs.q: To what height can a 400W engine lift a 100 kg mass in 3s?
mcqs.why: Formula: work done W = P t = m g h, so h = P t / (m g). Substitution: W = 400 x 3 = 1200 J, and h = 1200 / (100 x 9.8) = 1200 / 980. Step: 1200 / 980 = 1.22. Result: the engine can lift the mass through 1.22 m. Note: the book's printed answer of 0.122 m is wrong because it is ten times too small.

mcqs.q: A ball of mass 100 g is thrown vertically upward at a speed of 25 ms^-1. If no energy is lost, determine the height it would reach. If the ball only rises to 25m, calculate the work done against air resistance. Also calculate the force of friction. (Give the work done against air resistance.)
mcqs.why: Formula: work against air resistance = initial K.E. - P.E. at the height actually reached = (1/2) m v^2 - m g h. Substitution: initial K.E. = 0.5 x 0.1 x 25^2 = 31.25 J and P.E. at 25 m = 0.1 x 9.8 x 25 = 24.5 J. Step: 31.25 - 24.5 = 6.75. Result: work done against air resistance is about 6.7 J (the ball would have reached 31.9 m with no energy loss).

mcqs.q: A body of mass 'm' drops from Bridge into water of the river. The bridge is 10m high from the water surface. (a). Find the speed of the body 5m above the water surface. (b). Find the speed of the body before it strikes the water. (Give the speed of the body just before it strikes the water, part (b).)
mcqs.why: Formula: v = sqrt(2 g h) for a body dropped from rest through height h. Substitution: v = sqrt(2 x 9.8 x 10) = sqrt(196). Step: the square root of 196 is 14. Result: the body strikes the water at 14 m/s; halfway down, after falling 5 m, its speed is 9.9 m/s.

mcqs.q: The engine of a JF-Thunder fighter (made by Pakistan and China) develops a thrust of 3000N. What horsepower does it at a velocity of 600 m s^-1?
mcqs.why: Formula: power P = F v, then convert using 1 hp = 746 W. Substitution: P = 3000 x 600 = 1.8 x 10^6 W, and P in hp = (1.8 x 10^6) / 746. Step: 1.8 x 10^6 / 746 = 2413. Result: the engine develops 2413 hp at a velocity of 600 m/s.

mcqs.q: The mass of the moon is 1/80 of the mass of the earth and corresponding radius is 1/4 of the earth. Calculate the escape velocity on the surface of moon.
mcqs.why: Formula: v_esc = sqrt(2 G M / R), so v_moon / v_earth = sqrt((M_m / M_e) x (R_e / R_m)). Substitution: v_moon = 11.2 x sqrt((1/80) x (4/1)) = 11.2 x sqrt(0.05). Step: sqrt(0.05) = 0.2236, and 11.2 x 0.2236 = 2.50. Result: escape velocity on the surface of the Moon = 2.5 km/s.

lessons.title: Multiple Choice Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • The Earth rotates through 2 pi radians in 24 hours, giving an angular speed of pi/12 radians per hour.
  • In a = alpha x r, the angular acceleration vector and the radius vector are perpendicular to each other.
  • The moment of inertia of a solid sphere about its centre is (2/5) M R^2.
  • A constant force always perpendicular to the velocity makes a particle move in a circular path.
  • A body in uniform circular motion has constant speed but variable, centre-directed acceleration.
  • The angular momentum of a satellite in orbit remains constant because gravity exerts no torque about the centre.
  • The rotational kinetic energy of a rolling solid cylinder is one-third of its total kinetic energy.

Solved Exercises

Exercise - Multiple Choice Questions

Q: Q1. The angular speed in radians/hours for daily rotation of our earth is?

Options: (a) 2 pi (b) 4 pi (c) pi/6 (d) pi/12

Correct answer: pi/12

Q: Q2. Linear acceleration a = alpha x r. The angle between alpha and r is:

Options: (a) 0 degrees (b) 180 degrees (c) 360 degrees (d) 90 degrees

Correct answer: 90 degrees

Q: Q3. What is moment of inertia of a sphere?

Options: (a) M R^2 (b) (1/2) M R^2 (c) (2/5) M R^2 (d) (1/2) M^2 R

Correct answer: (2/5) M R^2

Q: Q4. A particle is acted upon by a force of constant magnitude which is always perpendicular to the velocity of particle. The motion of the particle takes place in a horizontal plane. It follows

Options: (a) Linear momentum is constant (b) Velocity is constant (c) It moves in a circular path (d) particle move in straight line

Correct answer: It moves in a circular path

Q: Q5. A body moving in a circular path with constant speed has

Options: (a) Constant acceleration (b) Constant retardation (c) Variable acceleration (d) Variable speed and constant velocity

Correct answer: Variable acceleration

Q: Q6. Astronauts appear weightless in space because

Options: (a) there is no gravity in space (b) there is no floor pushing upwards on the (c) satellite is freely falling (d) there is no air in space

Correct answer: satellite is freely falling

Q: Q7. Which one is constant for a satellite in orbit?

Options: (a) Velocity (b) K.E (c) Angular Momentum (d) Potential Energy

Correct answer: Angular Momentum

Q: Q8. If the earth suddenly stops rotating the value of 'g' at equator would:

Options: (a) Decrease (b) Remain unchanged (c) Increase (d) Become Zero

Correct answer: Increase

Q: Q9. If solid sphere and solid cylinder of same mass and density rotate about their own axis, the moment of inertia will be greater for

Options: (a) Solid sphere (b) Solid cylinder (c) The one that has the largest mass arrives first. (d) The one that has the largest radius arrives first.

Correct answer: Solid cylinder

Q: Q10. The gravitational force exerted on an astronaut on Earth's surface is 650N down. When she is in the International Space Station, the gravitational force on her is

Options: (a) larger (b) exactly the same (c) smaller (d) nearly but not exactly zero (e) exactly zero

Correct answer: smaller

Q: Q11. A solid cylinder of mass M and radius R rolls down an incline without slipping. Its moment of inertia about an axis through its center of mass is M R^2/2. At any instant while in motion, its rotational kinetic energy about its center of mass is what fraction of its total kinetic energy?

Options: (a) 1/2 (b) 1/4 (c) 1/3 (d) 2/5

Correct answer: 1/3

mcqs.q: The angular speed in radians/hours for daily rotation of our earth is?
mcqs.why: Earth completes one revolution of 2 pi radians in 24 hours, so the angular speed is 2 pi divided by 24, which equals pi/12 radians per hour.

mcqs.q: Linear acceleration a = alpha x r. The angle between alpha and r is:
mcqs.why: In the cross product a equals alpha cross r, the vectors alpha and r are perpendicular to each other, so the angle between them is 90 degrees.

mcqs.q: What is moment of inertia of a sphere?
mcqs.why: For a solid sphere the moment of inertia about an axis through its centre is two-fifths of M R squared, which matches the keyed option exactly.

mcqs.q: A particle is acted upon by a force of constant magnitude which is always perpendicular to the velocity of particle. The motion of the particle takes place in a horizontal plane. It follows
options: It moves in a circular path
mcqs.why: A constant force always perpendicular to the velocity changes only the direction of motion, so the particle is forced to move in a circular path.

mcqs.q: A body moving in a circular path with constant speed has
mcqs.why: The speed stays constant but the direction of velocity changes continuously, so the velocity changes and the body has variable, centripetal acceleration.

mcqs.q: Which one is constant for a satellite in orbit?
mcqs.why: For a satellite gravity provides the centripetal force with no torque about the centre, so its angular momentum about the centre remains constant.

mcqs.q: If the earth suddenly stops rotating the value of 'g' at equator would:
mcqs.why: Rotation reduces the effective g at the equator through the outward effect; if rotation stops that reduction vanishes and g at the equator would increase.

mcqs.q: If solid sphere and solid cylinder of same mass and density rotate about their own axis, the moment of inertia will be greater for
options: The one that has the largest mass arrives first.
The one that has the largest radius arrives first.
mcqs.why: For the same mass and radius form, the solid cylinder factor one-half exceeds the solid sphere factor two-fifths, so the cylinder has the greater moment of inertia.

mcqs.q: The gravitational force exerted on an astronaut on Earth's surface is 650N down. When she is in the International Space Station, the gravitational force on her is
mcqs.why: Gravity at the space station altitude is only slightly weaker than at the surface, so the force on the astronaut is smaller than 650 N but far from zero.

mcqs.q: A solid cylinder of mass M and radius R rolls down an incline without slipping. Its moment of inertia about an axis through its center of mass is M R^2/2. At any instant while in motion, its rotational kinetic energy about its center of mass is what fraction of its total kinetic energy?
mcqs.why: Rotational kinetic energy is one-quarter M v squared and total kinetic energy is three-quarters M v squared, so the rotational fraction is one-third of the total.

lessons.title: Short Answer Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • A heavy rim gives a flywheel a large moment of inertia, so it resists sudden changes in angular velocity and smooths engine motion.
  • Rifling spins the bullet, and conservation of angular momentum keeps it nose-first for a straighter, more accurate flight.
  • A raw egg wobbles and stops quickly when spun because its liquid interior lags behind and shifts about.
  • Centripetal acceleration points to the centre because the change in velocity between close positions points to the centre.
  • At the lowest point of a swing the tension equals m g + m v^2 / r, which can exceed the string's breaking strength.
  • Three geo-stationary satellites spaced 120 degrees apart are the minimum needed for global television coverage.
  • Apparent weight in a lift is m(g - a) for downward acceleration and becomes zero in free fall.

Solved Exercises

Exercise - Short Answer Questions

Q: Q1. Why is the fly wheel of an engine made heavy in the rim?

Ans: The rim carries most of the mass of the flywheel, far from the axis of rotation. This gives the flywheel a large moment of inertia, I = sum of m r^2, because r is large for the rim mass. A large moment of inertia resists sudden changes in angular velocity, so the flywheel stores rotational kinetic energy during the power stroke and releases it during the other strokes. The engine therefore runs smoothly at a nearly steady speed instead of jerking with every stroke.

Q: Q2. Why is a rifle barrel 'rifled'?

Ans: The inside of a rifle barrel is cut with spiral grooves, called rifling. As the bullet travels through the barrel, these grooves grip it and make it spin rapidly about its own long axis. The spinning bullet has angular momentum along its direction of flight. By conservation of angular momentum this spin keeps the bullet pointing nose-first and resists tumbling or turning aside in the air. The bullet therefore flies straighter and hits the target more accurately.

Q: Q3. Is it possible for a person to distinguish between a raw egg and a hard boiled one by spinning each on a table? Explain.

Ans: Yes. A hard boiled egg is solid throughout, so it spins smoothly and steadily for a long time like a rigid body. In a raw egg the liquid inside does not rotate with the shell at once; it lags behind, shifts about and disturbs the spin, so the raw egg wobbles and stops quickly. A second test also works: stop a spinning egg for an instant and release it. The boiled egg stays stopped, but the raw egg starts turning again because its liquid interior is still moving and drags the shell around.

Q: Q4. Why is the acceleration of a body moving uniformly in a circle, directed towards the centre?

Ans: In uniform circular motion the speed is constant but the direction of velocity changes at every point, and velocity is always tangent to the circle. The change in velocity, Delta v, between two close positions points towards the centre of the circle. Since acceleration is the rate of change of velocity, a = Delta v / Delta t, the acceleration also points towards the centre. This centripetal acceleration has magnitude a_c = v^2 / r and is produced by the centripetal force acting towards the centre.

Q: Q5. A ball is just supported by a string without breaking. If it is set swinging, it breaks. Why?

Ans: When the ball hangs at rest, the tension in the string is only equal to the weight of the ball, T = m g, which the string can just bear. When the ball is set swinging, at the lowest point of the swing the string must also provide the centripetal force for the circular motion. The tension becomes T = m g + m v^2 / r, which is greater than the weight alone. This extra tension exceeds the breaking strength of the string, so the string breaks.

Q: Q6. An insect is sitting close to the axis of a wheel. If the friction between the insect and the wheel is very small, describe the motion of the insect when the wheel starts rotating.

Ans: To rotate with the wheel, the insect needs friction to provide torque and centripetal force. Because friction is very small, almost no torque is transferred to the insect. The wheel therefore turns underneath it while the insect nearly stays in its original state, appearing to rotate backwards relative to the wheel. In practice it is dragged around only very slowly, lags far behind the wheel, and may slowly drift outwards because there is not enough friction to hold it in circular motion.

Q: Q7. Explain how many minimum number of geo-stationary satellites are required for global coverage of T.V transmission.

Ans: A geo-stationary satellite is parked at a height of about 35,790 km above the equator, where it orbits in 24 hours and appears fixed over one point of the Earth. From that height one satellite can send signals to only a limited part of the Earth, covering about 120 degrees of longitude. The full 360 degrees around the Earth therefore needs 360 / 120 = 3 satellites, placed 120 degrees apart in the geo-stationary orbit. So a minimum of three geo-stationary satellites is required for global T.V coverage.

Q: Q8. Explain the significance of moment of inertia in rotatory motion.

Ans: Moment of inertia is the rotational counterpart of mass in linear motion. It measures how much a body resists a change in its state of rotation: the torque needed to produce angular acceleration alpha is tau = I alpha, just as F = m a in linear motion. It depends not only on the total mass but also on how that mass is distributed about the axis, I = sum of m_i r_i^2, so mass farther from the axis counts more. It also fixes the rotational kinetic energy, K.E = (1/2) I omega^2, and the angular momentum, L = I omega, of the body.

Q: Q9. Why does the coasting rotating system slow down as water drops into the beaker?

Ans: The beaker is coasting, so no external torque acts on the system and its angular momentum L = I omega must stay constant. As water drops fall into the rotating beaker, they are caught by it and spread out, so the mass of the rotating system and its moment of inertia I increase. Since L = I omega is constant and I has increased, the angular velocity omega must decrease. The system therefore slows down as more water collects in the beaker.

Q: Q10. A body will be weightless when the elevator falls down just like a free falling body. Explain.
